articles.title: India rejects patent bid for treatment of drug-resistant TB
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Civil society groups urge U.S.-based Global Alliance for TB Drug Development to withdraw related patent claims in other countries

The Indian Patent Office has rejected a patent application filed by the U.S.-based Global Alliance for TB Drug Development (TB Alliance) for the combination of bedaquiline, pretomanid, and linezolid (BPaL), a six-month, all-oral treatment regimen for drug-resistant tuberculosis.
The Delhi Network of Positive People (DNP+), Sankalp Rehabilitation Trust and Third World Network (TWN) welcomed the development.
Recommended by the WHO for eligible people, BPaL offers a shorter course of treatment than older, longer regimens, reducing the burden of treatment on patients and their families.

“Only those who have been treated for TB know what it feels like to go through more than a year of antibiotics with painful injections. Access to a shorter, oral and effective treatment can mean returning to work, caring for their families and rebuilding their lives”, explained Loon Gangte of DNP+.

The decision follows two pre-grant oppositions filed in 2020—one by Eldred Tellis (Sankalp Rehabilitation Trust) and Ganesh Acharya, with support from the Lawyers’ Collective and Médécins Sans Frontières Access Campaign, and the other by the Delhi Network of Positive People (DNP+), with support from TWN.

The opponents challenged the patent application on the grounds that the combination of bedaquiline, pretomanid and linezolid, as well as its use in a shorter treatment regimen, had already been disclosed in scientific research and clinical trials dating back to 2015. They argued that combining these known medicines did not constitute an inventive step warranting a new patent monopoly.

The Opposition invoked key safeguards under India’s Patents Act, including Section 3(d), which restricts patents on new uses of known substances, Section 3(e), which excludes mere admixtures, and Section 3(i), which excludes methods of medical treatment. The opponents further argued that the application failed to sufficiently disclose the claimed invention. All four grounds were upheld by the Indian Patent Office.

India has the world’s largest tuberculosis burden. According to WHO estimates, approximately 2.71 million people developed TB in the country in 2024, accounting for a quarter of global cases, with an incidence rate of 187 per 1,00,000 people. Civil society groups are also demanding that the TB Alliance stop the pursuit of proprietary rights over BPaL in other countries.

“Having received public and philanthropic support to develop pretomanid, one of BPaL’s components, they should not be applying for a patent, let alone over frivolous secondary patents on its combination with the other two known medicines,” said Mr. Tellis.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment 📅 28 Oct 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

India rejects patent bid for treatment of drug-resistant TB

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports

Civil society groups urge U.S.-based Global Alliance for TB Drug Development to withdraw related patent claims in other countries

The Indian Patent Office has rejected a patent application filed by the U.S.-based Global Alliance for TB Drug Development (TB Alliance) for the combination of bedaquiline, pretomanid, and linezolid (BPaL), a six-month, all-oral treatment regimen for drug-resistant tuberculosis.

The Delhi Network of Positive People (DNP+), Sankalp Rehabilitation Trust and Third World Network (TWN) welcomed the development.

Recommended by the WHO for eligible people, BPaL offers a shorter course of treatment than older, longer regimens, reducing the burden of treatment on patients and their families.

“Only those who have been treated for TB know what it feels like to go through more than a year of antibiotics with painful injections. Access to a shorter, oral and effective treatment can mean returning to work, caring for their families and rebuilding their lives”, explained Loon Gangte of DNP+.

The decision follows two pre-grant oppositions filed in 2020—one by Eldred Tellis (Sankalp Rehabilitation Trust) and Ganesh Acharya, with support from the Lawyers’ Collective and Médécins Sans Frontières Access Campaign, and the other by the Delhi Network of Positive People (DNP+), with support from TWN.

The opponents challenged the patent application on the grounds that the combination of bedaquiline, pretomanid and linezolid, as well as its use in a shorter treatment regimen, had already been disclosed in scientific research and clinical trials dating back to 2015. They argued that combining these known medicines did not constitute an inventive step warranting a new patent monopoly.

The Opposition invoked key safeguards under India’s Patents Act, including Section 3(d), which restricts patents on new uses of known substances, Section 3(e), which excludes mere admixtures, and Section 3(i), which excludes methods of medical treatment. The opponents further argued that the application failed to sufficiently disclose the claimed invention. All four grounds were upheld by the Indian Patent Office.

India has the world’s largest tuberculosis burden. According to WHO estimates, approximately 2.71 million people developed TB in the country in 2024, accounting for a quarter of global cases, with an incidence rate of 187 per 1,00,000 people. Civil society groups are also demanding that the TB Alliance stop the pursuit of proprietary rights over BPaL in other countries.

Patents on the BPaL combination have been granted in 11 countries and are set to expire in 2036: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bulgaria, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, South Africa, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan.

articles.title: Vehicle data shared only in masked form: ULIP
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Clarification comes after Road Ministry sought audit of users accessing the Centre’s logistics portal following complaints that multiple apps and websites are selling vehicle information

After the Road Ministry sought an audit of users accessing the Centre’s logistics portal following complaints that multiple apps and websites were selling vehicle information, the Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP) rejected the allegations of its misuse. It said all data were masked and called for broader scrutiny of the platforms involved.

“ULIP relays information in the format received from the source API. For example, vehicle owner names, chassis and engine numbers retain their masking, and the mobile number field remains null in both the source response and the response provided to users. ULIP does not independently generate, unmask or enrich the underlying data,” ULIP wrote in response to a story in The Hindu .

The Road Ministry sought an audit after finding that some entities were extracting data in large volumes from ULIP with some as many pulling out as many as 50 lakh records a month. The Road Ministry shares vehicle information with multiple government agencies and private firms from its portals such as VAHAN, SARATHI, e-Challan and PUCC portals.

ULIP says it uses sufficient safeguards that include screening of entities that have access to its portal, their proposed use cases, binding terms and conditions, IP whitelisting, phased onboarding and continuous monitoring of API usage. This framework complies with the Road Ministry’s Policy for Data Sharing from the National Transport Repository, which prescribes authentication, secret keys, masking of personally identifiable information (PII) and defined approval mechanisms, ULIP added.

Referring to multiple apps selling vehicle information data in unmasked form, ULIP said there needed to be a “scrutiny of wider ecosystem of platforms and channels through which such information is being made available”.

The Road Ministry has written to the government’s nodal agency for investigating cybersecurity incidents, Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), seeking a forensic audit of VAHAN, SARATHI, e-Challan and PUCC portals, which hold a range of vehicle-owner information.

It has also sought the intervention of the Ministry of Electronics and Information and Technology (MEITY) for a review of its data sharing policy and suggest ways to strengthen it. The Road Ministry also plans to audit various enforcement agencies that access its portals for data.

The Ministry’s action follows reports that apps and websites were selling vehicle-linked personal data for as little as ₹5. A Cyderes investigation found that a Telegram-based broker could retrieve an owner’s name, contact details, addresses and other records from a vehicle registration number, along with driving licence, challan, FASTag and registration certificate information. The Ministry has asked major app-store operators, including Google, to remove such apps.

articles.title: How imaging offers a window to treat wake-up strokes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: One in five ischaemic strokes is a wake-up stroke. “This means a person wakes up from his/her sleep with symptoms of stroke. The symptoms include facial drooping, difficulty speaking, sudden vision problems and weakness on one side of the body

Time is brain, when it comes to the treatment of strokes. But a stroke occurring during sleep may go unnoticed until a person wakes up with symptoms, leaving doctors without a clear timeline of its onset. This is where brain imaging helps doctors identify patients with wake-up strokes and assess the extent of injury to pave the way for prompt treatment. Neurologists underscore the need to seek medical care immediately to ensure timely treatment.

M. Radha, head of department and professor of neurology, Government Kilpauk Medical College (KMC) Hospital, Chennai, said that the prevalence of wake-up strokes is 20% - one in five ischaemic strokes is a wake-up stroke. “This means a person wakes up from his/her sleep with symptoms of stroke. The symptoms include facial drooping, difficulty speaking, sudden vision problems and weakness on one side of the body,” she said.

If a patient arrives at a hospital within 4.5 hours of stroke symptoms, then thrombolysis can be done, she said, adding: “However, in wake-up stroke, we cannot calculate the time of the onset of symptoms. We do not know the window. So, acting fast is important. In case of any symptoms, patients should reach the hospital on time.”

In wake-up strokes, imaging helps give a clear picture for the doctors. “An MRI brain scan should be taken immediately. If it is not available, a CT angiogram should be taken. The scans help us assess the extent of brain injury and blood flow to different parts of the brain. They can determine whether there is diffusion-perfusion mismatch. The difference may represent brain tissue that is still salvageable and can be potentially saved. Like in regular strokes, ‘time is brain’ in wake-up strokes too, making prompt diagnosis and treatment crucial,” she explained.

Shubha Subramanian, senior consultant - neurology, Kauvery Hospitals, Chennai, said that in ischemic strokes, thrombolysis is used to dissolve the blood clot if a patient presents within 4.5 hours of symptom onset. “In cases involving a large vessel occlusion, mechanical thrombectomy is performed within 24 hours of symptom onset, depending on the patient’s eligibility. In wake-up strokes, we do not know when the stroke started; it could be at night or early in the morning. What we do next is crucial. This is why we rely on imaging techniques,” she added.

“MRI has a lot of sequences. If you compare the diffusion-weighted imaging and FLAIR (Fluid-Attenuated Inversion Recovery) imaging, a mismatch in that shows that the brain tissue is still salvageable. So even if we do not know the time of onset of stroke, we can still go ahead and thrombolyse the patient. In the same way, MRI perfusion or CT perfusion studies will also give us a clue regarding salvageable brain tissue. This will help us in taking crucial decisions regarding thrombolysis or mechanical thrombectomy or whether to go for conservative management,” she elaborated.

Under the Tamil Nadu Accident and Emergency Care Initiative and Stroke Care and Rapid Intervention with Plasminogen activator and Thrombectomy (SCRIPT) programme implemented by the Tamil Nadu government and with facilities available at the new JICA building at KMC, patients with with wake-up strokes are regularly treated, Dr. Radha noted.

“There is effective coordination between the administration, the emergency department, radiology and neurology departments. We have a green channel in place. As a result, once the patients with symptoms of stroke enter the Emergency Department, the neurologist is intimated. Our doctor goes to the radiology department which has significantly reduced the door to needle time,” she said.

BE FAST is the acronym to spot the warning signs of stroke, denoting Balance, Eyes, Face, Arm, Speech and Time. “We do see that the awareness of stroke symptoms is increasing and the referral system has also improved,” Dr. Radha said.

Dr. Shubha Subramanian said that in wake-up strokes, the person may not realise that he/she has symptoms of stroke when they wake up from sleep. “They may face difficulty in getting up and may also fall as a result. It is important for family members to identify the symptoms and rush for medical help,” she added.

articles.title: Star Wars Galactic Racer’s roguelike racing mechanics is not for all
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Any racing game with a high-risk nitro booster called RamJet, is a game you need to play right now, and Star Wars Galactic Racer has plenty of it

Ask anyone what the best part of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace is, and every one of them will say the thunderous, high-octane chaos-filled, pod racing sequence. Now, ask anyone what their favourite arcade-style racing game is, and the Burnout series will pretty much be high up on that list.

Burnout was a racing game built around spectacular car crashes, back when burnout meant wrecking cars rather than your mental health. Now, fuse both Episode 1 Racer and Burnout — the chaos, speed and fiddly unpredictability of racing hovering death traps across the galaxy with aggressive vehicular destruction, and you get Star Wars Galactic Racer . Fuse Games, made up of former Burnout developers, has delivered the insanity.

Everyone knows a Kestar Bool in their circles — the spoiled rich kid who makes sure everyone is pushed down so he can succeed. He has been trained by Sebulba (who folks will recognise from The Phantom Menace , as the evil champion of the pod racing circuit), who has passed not only his racing skills to Kestar, but also his nasty ways.

You play as Shade who is tasked with taking down Kestar’s toxic dominance in the Galactic League, a high-stakes illegal racing circuit where many of the top pilots have a place to earn big bucks after the Empire fell. A story that feels quite Star Wars with a healthy dash of Fast and the Furious with aliens, robots and anti-gravity cars.

The game features a Forza Horizon -esque opening sequence that is every bit as cinematic, allowing you to take control of several types of repulsorcraft, which is the fancy sci-fi name for these floating vehicles. The story usually unfolds in quiet walkabout encampment areas where you get to interact with your opponents in a more stationary setting.

It also gives you a chance to speak to various memorable characters, interact with your cute monkey-like mechanic Hibi, and the founder of the League Darius Pax, a mechanic himself and the person who has brought on Shade to help him deal with Kestar. Once you are all storied up, the action then shifts to the high-speed arenas of the Galactic League.

Star Wars Episode 1 Racer was one of the best games of its time when it came out, and it still holds up today. Even if its graphics are dated, the screams, whines and mechanical shivers of those giant engines powering through levels will always be burned in your brain.

There are four distinct types of repulsorcraft you get to scream around corners with — the trusty, souped-up variants of the Landspeeder, which are big, fast moving slabs that look and handle like muscle cars, with a proper drift. Then, there are the speeder bikes, which have absolutely no protection for the rider, but possess a cool kinetic burst-through that swings you out of corners.

The Skim Speeder gives Sony’s Wipeout racing feels with its extended fins and is designed to go very fast, with an ability to tilt vertically to fit through tight gaps. And lastly, there is the return of the Pod Racer, which you only get to pilot in certain events, sadly. Pod Racers are like chariots, but instead of being drawn by horses, they are pulled by massive engines.

These craft absolutely rip through incredible courses. This game is built on aggressive speed and constant danger, and I love how unpredictable the races are. There were moments I was absolutely sure I was going to finish sixth, but after some clever turns and punting a few opponents into oncoming debris, I netted myself a near first. You have to race dirty, pulling off your special moves like forcefields to gain every edge. Managing your boost is key — spit out too much and your craft is going to be panting.
The game introduces a lovely feature called RamJet, which is a secondary-state boost that adds a lot of risk, but if done right you can punch further.

The best part of the whole pod racing sequence is when Anakin’s pod starts malfunctioning, and he has to fiddle with switches to redirect power, fix the kaput engine, then run a very cool-looking, firing up sequence even as the pod is running at a mindblowing speed.

Now, fuse both Episode 1 Racer and Burnout — the chaos, speed and fiddly unpredictability of racing hovering death traps across the galaxy with aggressive vehicular destruction, and you get Star Wars Galactic Racer . Fuse Games, made up of former Burnout developers, has delivered the insanity.

Everyone knows a Kestar Bool in their circles — the spoiled rich kid who makes sure everyone is pushed down so he can succeed. He has been trained by Sebulba (who folks will recognise from The Phantom Menace , as the evil champion of the pod racing circuit), who has passed not only his racing skills to Kestar, but also his nasty ways.

You play as Shade who is tasked with taking down Kestar’s toxic dominance in the Galactic League, a high-stakes illegal racing circuit where many of the top pilots have a place to earn big bucks after the Empire fell. A story that feels quite Star Wars with a healthy dash of Fast and the Furious with aliens, robots and anti-gravity cars.

The game features a Forza Horizon -esque opening sequence that is every bit as cinematic, allowing you to take control of several types of repulsorcraft, which is the fancy sci-fi name for these floating vehicles. The story usually unfolds in quiet walkabout encampment areas where you get to interact with your opponents in a more stationary setting.

It also gives you a chance to speak to various memorable characters, interact with your cute monkey-like mechanic Hibi, and the founder of the League Darius Pax, a mechanic himself and the person who has brought on Shade to help him deal with Kestar. Once you are all storied up, the action then shifts to the high-speed arenas of the Galactic League.

Star Wars Episode 1 Racer was one of the best games of its time when it came out, and it still holds up today. Even if its graphics are dated, the screams, whines and mechanical shivers of those giant engines powering through levels will always be burned in your brain.

There are four distinct types of repulsorcraft you get to scream around corners with — the trusty, souped-up variants of the Landspeeder, which are big, fast moving slabs that look and handle like muscle cars, with a proper drift. Then, there are the speeder bikes, which have absolutely no protection for the rider, but possess a cool kinetic burst-through that swings you out of corners.

The Skim Speeder gives Sony’s Wipeout racing feels with its extended fins and is designed to go very fast, with an ability to tilt vertically to fit through tight gaps. And lastly, there is the return of the Pod Racer, which you only get to pilot in certain events, sadly. Pod Racers are like chariots, but instead of being drawn by horses, they are pulled by massive engines.

These craft absolutely rip through incredible courses. This game is built on aggressive speed and constant danger, and I love how unpredictable the races are. There were moments I was absolutely sure I was going to finish sixth, but after some clever turns and punting a few opponents into oncoming debris, I netted myself a near first. You have to race dirty, pulling off your special moves like forcefields to gain every edge. Managing your boost is key — spit out too much and your craft is going to be panting.

The game introduces a lovely feature called RamJet, which is a secondary-state boost that adds a lot of risk, but if done right you can punch further.

The best part of the whole pod racing sequence is when Anakin’s pod starts malfunctioning, and he has to fiddle with switches to redirect power, fix the kaput engine, then run a very cool-looking, firing up sequence even as the pod is running at a mindblowing speed.

articles.title: Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen is a massive improvement over the original
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Send your pawns that back-to-work notice because Dark Arisen, the new expansion of Dragon Dogma 2, has a new area to explore and a whole host of improvements in tow

This October is turning out to be a case of thanking yourself for holding out on playing certain open world games, starting with the Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition which launched on October 1, 2026 with its new expansion that made the game complete. Now it is the turn of 2024’s Dragon Dogma 2; Dark Arisen that not only brings a massive new area, but also fixes quite a lot of the original’s flaws.

Capcom surprising gamers with a sequel to one of their lesser known, but much loved open world RPG’s Dragon’s Dogma, which is now getting a massive expansion, convinces us of the house of Resident Evil ’s motives to make sure all its IPs get the right treatment.

Welcome to Norgon, a cut-off frigid northern land that is harsh, cold and full of unforgiving monsters. At the centre of it all, there is a mysterious new entity known as a Fallen Dragon, that you as an Arisen and your trusty pawns must travel to. Inspired by Norse and Celtic mythology and influences, Norgon may be a smaller region than the main game’s sprawling kingdom, but it has got heights to scale and unknowns lurking in dark ruins.

Guided by a mysterious wanderer Eir, Dark Arisen switches up the political intrigue to a more ancient evil with deeper answers into the dark side of the cosmic cycle that lies at the heart of this world.

But, wait! Norse influence, dragons, cold mountains and ruins, is that you Skyrim? Yes, there is some of that Skyrim vibe to Norgon in there, but it is just atmosphere. The story feels right in Dark Arisen — it is short, focused and has a few memorable characters. Addressing some of the feedback from the original base game, which had a lot of half-baked, Game of Thrones -type stuff happening (read royal conspiracies and political intrigue), Dark Arisen has a strong, fairly linear, mystery at its core. Eir’s role in all this paints quite a picture.
The peeling off those layers to uncover that mystery as you go along is done well, with clear motives laid out for all its strong characters.

One of the strong points of Dragon’s Dogma is in its action system, where you play an Arisen, a being chosen by a dragon by tearing out your heart. This gives you the ability to pull out pawns from a space called the Rift, leaving you a steady source of party members with ready knowledge of other player’s games.

While you have your main pawn as your companion, you can balance your party out with the ones that offset your weaknesses or you can use them as fodder. Dark Arisen pawns however, come with two extra active weapon skills that bump them up from four to six, with skill options. This matters a lot because you do not just craft individual builds, but design complete party wide synergies.

This versatility can let you experiment more while dealing with the fresh monsters and enemies you encounter in this new area. The pawn system, coupled with an excellent fighting system, is what makes Dragon Dogma 2 really sing, especially when you get your builds right. You can now start melting monsters on sight, which was also one of the big problems of the base game.

Norgon functions as a high-level zone, and as a result, you are at the bottom of the food chain again, so you need to grind to get better weapons. This is good because the challenge of facing off and defeating monsters is back. If you have been playing the base game, hitting level 30 automatically puts you into a power fantasy and it can get boring. Monsters now are tougher and you will need to choose the right classes to stand a chance.

Thankfully, there are a lot of side quests and ruins to explore to net relic weapons. Another point of note, there have been multiple patches before Dark Arisen that have massively balanced and optimised the main game, so if you are starting anew, it is not a bad idea. However, it is worth remembering that no amount of patching fixes the main campaign’s insipid slog of a story.

Enemies are tougher, and in the expansion as well, the game seems to regurgitate similar enemy types throughout, though there is some variety, which was one of the big issues of the main game too. But, what the game lacks in variety it makes up for in dropped weapons called relics.

articles.title: Wicked surprise: On the northeast monsoon
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The northeast monsoon is more unpredictable, and the south must be wary

As India recovers from a monsoon-deficit year , there is both hope and trepidation regarding the prospects for that ‘other monsoon’, or the ‘northeast monsoon’ . While contributing only around a quarter of India’s annual rainfall, it is largely focused on the south-east peninsula regions of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, coastal Andhra Pradesh, Rayalaseema, south interior Karnataka and Keralam. The southwest monsoon, influenced by a strengthening El Niño , has already left its desiccating mark. Rainfall from June-September was 759.4 mm against 868.6 mm, a 12.6% deficit, the driest in 11 years. This has impacted kharif sowing and is reflected in food inflation.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that this year, the northeast monsoon rainfall, spanning October to December, would likely be ‘normal’ , meaning in line with a 50-year average and within a 12% error window. Most parts of the country, it said, are expected to receive below-normal rainfall, except some areas of northwest India and southern parts of peninsular India, where rainfall is likely to be normal to above-normal. The wide error window, however, is far less precise than its forecasts for the southwest monsoon with its margin of 5%, and can sometimes make the northeast monsoon the bearer of nasty surprises. For instance, December 1, 2015, saw the city of Chennai deluged by its heaviest rainfall in 24-hours in over a century ; at least 500 lives were lost and 18 lakh people displaced in the State. That year and the present are linked by a common thread: a powerful El Niño. Associated with the heating up of the Central Pacific, the El Niño is linked to the drying up of the southwest monsoon rains but also yoked — not always — with a vigorous northeast monsoon. Other than in 2015, several El Niño years, such as 1997 and 2009, have been associated with above-normal rainfall between October and December in Tamil Nadu though El Niño years, such as 2002 and 1982, saw a poor northeast monsoon (and a predictably bad southwest monsoon). While the climate mechanisms linking a vigorous northeast monsoon and El Niño are still to be fully understood, it appears the warming patterns of the El Niño tend to deflect rain-bearing cyclonic circulations in unpredictable ways. Therefore, the Centre and the southern States ought to take enough precautions: from clearing up stormwater drains, fortifying shelters, making provisions for infrastructure damage and tightening weather warning forecasts to prepare for torrents.

articles.title: Hunker down: On Cyclone Arnab, its landfall
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Proactive governance kept the casualties low after Cyclone Arnab

Cyclone Arnab, the first named storm of the North Indian Ocean cyclone season this year, intensified rapidly before making landfall as a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ on October 28. This particular rapidity is a challenge for forecasters and some models did fail to anticipate how strong Arnab would become. It also moved faster than expected towards the coast, before stalling for a time and beginning the landfall process several hours before the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had predicted it would, in the middle of the night, leaving many district authorities with a potentially narrower window to evacuate high-risk settlements. With core wind speeds of 125-135 kilometres per hour, it delivered more than 100 mm of rain over parts of Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Kalingapatnam, Kakinada and Machilipatnam, in Andhra Pradesh. But even though it has completed landfall, southern Odisha likely faces a greater threat only hence. Early reports claimed no loss of life in Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, which has been attributed to the disaster management operations in both States; the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, N. Chandrababu Naidu, said there were five deaths in Andhra Pradesh . Regrettably, the suspension of transport services, including road connectivity and flights, closure of schools and offices, and power cuts to minimise risks posed by loose wires remains an essential part of saving lives, entailing other social and economic disruptions that the States must account for, and address, in their post-storm assessments.

Odisha may have to brace for rainfall and waters due to moisture in the storm’s outer circulation, which will arrive over land that has recovered in patches from the fourth wettest monsoon in the State’s history. Extreme rainfall after repeated flooding may face soil that has not drained fully, raising the risk of more flooding following even lower levels of rainfall, and slope failures in hilly terrain. Farmers in Ganjam and Puri have already voiced worries about the risk of prolonged inundation destroying paddy crops, compounding the already considerable financial consequences of the southwest monsoon; Ganjam alone had lost 33% of crops by October. In Sundargarh, however, farmers hope that Arnab will relieve moisture stress in standing crops after a dry month. The IMD has already issued alerts in the Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, and Kalahandi districts, before the rainbelt extends further north. The relatively low figure of deaths will be a testament to proactive governance. However, it is past time that States adopted a zero-disruption approach, especially since property and infrastructure were damaged, and the risk of people being pushed into poverty over lost possessions and livelihoods persists.

Hunker down: On Cyclone Arnab, its landfall

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary

Proactive governance kept the casualties low after Cyclone Arnab

Cyclone Arnab, the first named storm of the North Indian Ocean cyclone season this year, intensified rapidly before making landfall as a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ on October 28. This particular rapidity is a challenge for forecasters and some models did fail to anticipate how strong Arnab would become. It also moved faster than expected towards the coast, before stalling for a time and beginning the landfall process several hours before the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had predicted it would, in the middle of the night, leaving many district authorities with a potentially narrower window to evacuate high-risk settlements. With core wind speeds of 125-135 kilometres per hour, it delivered more than 100 mm of rain over parts of Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Kalingapatnam, Kakinada and Machilipatnam, in Andhra Pradesh. But even though it has completed landfall, southern Odisha likely faces a greater threat only hence. Early reports claimed no loss of life in Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, which has been attributed to the disaster management operations in both States; the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, N. Chandrababu Naidu, said there were five deaths in Andhra Pradesh . Regrettably, the suspension of transport services, including road connectivity and flights, closure of schools and offices, and power cuts to minimise risks posed by loose wires remains an essential part of saving lives, entailing other social and economic disruptions that the States must account for, and address, in their post-storm assessments.

Odisha may have to brace for rainfall and waters due to moisture in the storm’s outer circulation, which will arrive over land that has recovered in patches from the fourth wettest monsoon in the State’s history. Extreme rainfall after repeated flooding may face soil that has not drained fully, raising the risk of more flooding following even lower levels of rainfall, and slope failures in hilly terrain. Farmers in Ganjam and Puri have already voiced worries about the risk of prolonged inundation destroying paddy crops, compounding the already considerable financial consequences of the southwest monsoon; Ganjam alone had lost 33% of crops by October. In Sundargarh, however, farmers hope that Arnab will relieve moisture stress in standing crops after a dry month. The IMD has already issued alerts in the Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, and Kalahandi districts, before the rainbelt extends further north. The relatively low figure of deaths will be a testament to proactive governance. However, it is past time that States adopted a zero-disruption approach, especially since property and infrastructure were damaged, and the risk of people being pushed into poverty over lost possessions and livelihoods persists.

articles.title: Clinging on: On Netanyahu and the Israel elections
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Netanyahu’s continuance will be bad news for Israel and the region

Benjamin Netanyahu was at the centre of Israel’s October 27 elections. For Israel’s longest-serving Prime Minister, who oversaw a genocidal war in Gaza following Hamas’s October 7 attack , the election was the biggest test of his political career. For the Opposition, which promised to hold him accountable for the failures of October 7 and end the country’s “forever wars”, the election offered an opportunity to oust him from power. The results, however, sent a mixed message. With 85.6% of the votes counted, Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition has lost its majority but is still the largest bloc . His Likud party is projected to win 26 seats, while its main rival Yashar, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, is expected to secure 21. Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism, the far-right extremist parties in Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition, demonstrated their continued strength, winning 13 seats between them. The dark horse, however, could be the Arab parties — the Joint List is projected to win 12 seats while the United Arab List (Ra’am) could secure seven seats. With neither bloc commanding a majority, the Arab parties could propel the opposition coalition to power. But the big question is whether the anti-Netanyahu coalition is ready to join hands with the Arab parties, which have historically been kept on the margins of Israel’ s power politics.

Mr. Netanyahu’s central promise has been that only he can guarantee Israel’s security. Yet, the October 7 attack took place on his watch and he has refused to take responsibility for the failures that led to it. A wanted man by the International Criminal Court, he has repeated, before and after October 7, that a Palestine state would not be formed while he is in power. His war on Gaza has killed over 70,000 Palestinians, including 20,000 children, and displaced the region’s population. Israel’s brutal occupation machinery has also expanded and tightened its control of the West Bank, while settler terrorists have unleashed violence on Palestinian households. His war on Iran has been a disaster, with global economic consequences. Mr. Netanyahu has sought to portray his wars as bold, necessary moves to protect Israel, while exploiting Israelis’ security concerns for political gain. He may not be voted out immediately, but his failure to secure a majority and the decline in his party’s popularity are significant. The Opposition should take its cue from the results and form a broad coalition with the Arab parties. It should restore accountability in governance, revisit his unchecked militarism and rebuild ties with the world. If Mr. Netanyahu continues to cling to power, it would be bad news for Israel and the region.

articles.title: New Collectors for Karur, Tiruppur and Tenkasi as T.N. government opts for bureaucratic reshuffle
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a bureaucratic reshuffle, the Tamil Nadu government has transferred C. Muthukumaran, District Collector, Karur, and posted him as District Collector, Tiruppur, replacing Manish S. Narnaware, who has been appointed Managing Director of Tamil Nadu FibreNet Corporation Limited.
S. Prasanna Ramasamy, Deputy Secretary to Governor (Universities), Lok Bhavan, Chennai, has been appointed District Collector, Karur, replacing C. Muthukumaran.

S.P. Karthikaa, Chief Executive Officer, Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority, has been transferred and posted as Additional Secretary, Social Welfare and Women Empowerment, replacing S. Valarmathi, who has been appointed Director, Rehabilitation and Welfare of Non-Resident Tamils.

R. Sadheesh, Director, Rehabilitation and Welfare of Non-Resident Tamils, has been transferred and posted as Director, Sericulture, Salem. Monica Rana, Commissioner, Tirunelveli Corporation, has been transferred and posted as District Collector, Tenkasi, replacing Ranjeet Singh.

M. Indhumathi, Chief Administrative Officer, Koyambedu Market Management Committee, Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority, has been transferred and posted as Deputy Secretary, Transport Department.

S. Sangeetha, District Revenue Officer, Amma Unavagam, Greater Chennai Corporation, has been appointed Director-cum-Mission Director, Integrated Child Development Services, Chennai, replacing K. Santhi, who has been appointed Managing Director, Overseas Manpower Corporation Limited.

N. Kalidoss, Zonal Officer-10, Greater Chennai Corporation, has been transferred and posted as Additional Director (General), Directorate of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj, Chennai. R. Venkateshwaran, Sub-Collector, Karur Division, has been transferred and posted as Sub-Collector, Chidambaram Division, Cuddalore district, replacing M. Subadharshini, who is on maternity leave.

R. Priya, Managing Director, Subramania Siva Cooperative Sugar Mills Limited, Dharmapuri, has been appointed Managing Director, Salem Starch and Sago Manufacturers’ Service Industrial Co-operative Society Limited (SAGOSERVE), replacing R. Keerthy Priyadharshini.

R. Rajakirubakaran, General Manager (Procurement), Electronics Corporation of Tamil Nadu Limited (ELCOT), has been appointed Executive Director, ELCOT. K. Priya, Joint Director (Technical), Directorate of e-Governance, has been appointed Commissioner, Tirunelveli Corporation, replacing Monica Rana.

M. Manimegalai, General Manager, Tamil Nadu Ex-Servicemen Corporation (TEXCO), has been appointed Vice-Chairman and Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Watershed Development Agency, replacing R. Kannan, who was holding additional charge.

A. Meena Priya Dharshini, Joint Director, Directorate of Children Welfare and Special Services, has been appointed Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Small Tea Growers’ Industrial Cooperative Tea Factories Federation Limited (INDCOSERVE), Coonoor, replacing Raja Gopal Sunkara.

T. Sengottaiyan, Special District Revenue Officer (Land Acquisition), Highways Department, has been appointed Chief Executive Officer, Chennai Metro Asset Management Limited (CMAML), replacing Sweta Suman. S. Shanthi, Joint Commissioner, Commissionerate of Prohibition and Excise, has been appointed Chief Executive Officer, Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority, replacing S.P. Karthikaa.

articles.title: CM to release book co-authored by late B. Madhusoodana Kurup
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will release a book co-authored by the late B. Madhusoodana Kurup, founder Vice-Chancellor of the Kerala University of Fisheries and Ocean Studies and former Director of the School of Industrial Fisheries, Cusat, at a function in Kochi on Friday (October 29, 2026).
The book, Exploring the Legacy of Fishing and Farming Below Sea Level: Vembanad-Kole Wetlands of Southern India , has been co-authored by Dr. Kurup and Dr. Sileesh Mullasseri.

The School of Industrial Fisheries, Cusat, will organise the function in memory of Dr. Kurup. Fisheries Minister V.E. Abdul Gafoor will preside over the event, which will be held at BTH Hotel at 3.15 p.m.
Former Fisheries Ministers K. Babu and S. Sharma will receive the first copies of the book.

articles.title: NTK’s ‘Saattai’ Duraimurugan moves Madras High Court seeking anticipatory bail
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: An FIR had been registered against him for his alleged derogatory YouTube video against Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and Minister Aadhav Arjuna

Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK) office-bearer A. Duraimurugan alias ‘Saattai’ Duraimurugan has approached the Madras High Court seeking anticipatory bail in a case booked against him by the Chennai cyber crime wing for having posted a defamatory video against Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and Minister for Public Works and Sports Development Aadhav Arjuna.

The plea has been listed for hearing before Justice N. Ramesh on Thursday (October 29, 2026). The First Information Report (FIR) had been registered on the basis of a complaint lodged by the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) cadre A. Christopher, a fisherman by profession, of Tondiarpet, in Chennai, on October 3, 2026. The complaint was related to a specific YouTube video uploaded on September 30, 2026.

The complainant said, the NTK office-bearer, also an YouTuber, had made derogatory remarks against the Minister for having addressed him as his younger brother. Further, the advance bail petitioner had made unsubstantiated allegations against the ruling government and accused it of having done nothing during its “honeymoon period” of 143 days since it assumed power in the State.

On the other hand, the petitioner dubbed the allegations made against him in the complaint as false and politically motivated. He said, the FIR had been registered to curb the freedom of speech and expression and scuttle democratic dissent. He contended that his YouTube video contained only a decent political constructive cricitism against the State government in the interest of people at large.

“As a political leader, the petitioner has a duty towards the welfare of the people of Tamil Nadu,” Mr. Duraimurugan said and accused the TVK cadre of having lodged a complaint against him without any locus standi. He claimed that the FIR had been registered with the intention of removing the contentious YouTube video from social media platforms since it damages the image of the ruling party.

Claiming that the case does not require his custodial interrogation and that he had already appeared for police inquiry, the petitioner said, he was willing to cooperate with the investigation and appear for inquiries in the future too.

articles.title: SAD-AAP trade barbs on drug menace issue in Punjab
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia accused Arvind Kejriwal of misleading Punjabis by giving the disproportionate assets case the label of a drug case to suppress the issue

With the drug menace issue emerging as the key poll issue ahead of the 2027 Assembly election, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) were embroiled in sharp war of words.

After the Punjab Vigilance Bureau filed a supplementary chargesheet against senior SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia in a disproportionate assets case before a special court in Mohali, AAP supremo and former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal said that the AAP government in Punjab is taking the fight against drugs to its conclusion by filing a chargesheet against Mr. Majithia.

Party’s Punjab in-charge Manish Sisodia said, “..The chargesheet filed by the Punjab Police against Bikram Singh Majithia today details how he earned ₹736 crore by selling drugs and deposited the money in bank accounts of his companies. After this chargesheet, Majithia will rot in jail for the rest of his life.”

Hitting out at the AAP, Mr. Majithia accused Mr. Kejriwal of misleading Punjabis by giving the disproportionate assets (DA) case the label of a drug case to suppress the issue of Punjab being pushed into turmoil.

“Mr. Kejriwal was attempting to divert public attention from the situation in Punjab by presenting the case against him as a drug trafficking case,” he said. He added that Mr. Kejriwal had apologised in 2018 for making false allegations against him in connection with drugs. “The AAP leadership was now once again trying to link his name to the drug case for political gains. The Supreme Court had given the government time until March 18, 2025, to establish the allegations against him, but the Kejriwal and Bhagwant Mann governments had failed to do so,” he said.

articles.title: 20 units of illegally mined sand near Ambur seized
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Officials said that the revenue earned in the public auction will go to the State exchequer
More than 20 units of river sand that was illegally mined from the dry Malattaru River was found at Machampattu village on Wednesday.

Revenue officials said that based on information from farmer and social activist J. Paranthaman, a team of revenue officials and the police inspected a private open land near the river, where huge quantities of river sand were stored in the open.

“Based on preliminary assessment, we have found over 20 units of river sand illegally kept in the private land. We have sealed the premises for further inspection by the Water Resources Department (WRD) team, for public auction of the seized sand,” S. Devi, Tasildar (Pernambut), told The Hindu.

A farming village, Machampattu forms part of Pernambut Panchayat Union in Vellore district. Most of the farmers depend on the river for domestic consumption and irrigation purposes. “Over the years, illegal sand mining has turned the perennial river into a seasonal waterbody. Illegal sand mining in the river also depleted groundwater in surrounding farming villages,” Mr. Paranthaman said.
Along with the local police, revenue officials led by tahsildar Devi had inspected the site where they found a large quantity of river sand stored in the open.

Revenue officials said that as per norms, mining of river sand, including for government purposes like construction of school buildings and Anganwadi centres, is prohibited in the State. For government infrastructure works, sand could be procured at designated government sand quarries in the district.

Revenue officials said that the revenue earned in the public auction will go to the State exchequer. Legal action will also be taken on the landowner, identified as Navin, for illegal mining of river sand. A probe is under way.

articles.title: TN Teachers Education University gets new Registrar-in-charge following allegation of irregularities by civilian group
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Welcoming the move, M. Radhakrishnan of Arappor Iyakkam, in a statement, demanded a thorough and transparent investigation into the complaint and legal action against those involved in the “fraud”

The Higher Education Department has appointed M. Kanmani, Dean, Department of Educational Technology, Tamil Nadu Teachers Education University (TNTEU) as the Registrar-in-charge after the incumbent Registrar was removed following allegations of irregularities by corruption watch group, Arappor Iyakkam.

In a notification issued by the TNTEU on October 26, the appointment of Prof. Kanmani was announced “consequent to the relieving of Dr. K. Rajasekaran on 26.10.2026 ... from the post of Registrar i/c of this University”. Arappor Iyakkam had, earlier this month, alleged discrepancies in the affiliation inspection process conducted during the 2023-24 and 2024-25 academic years.
Welcoming the move, M. Radhakrishnan of Arappor Iyakkam, in a statement, demanded a thorough and transparent investigation into the complaint and legal action against those involved in the “fraud”.

Additionally, the organisation insisted on publishing full details, including photographs, of faculty members working in affiliated colleges on the university’s website, to prohibit the practice of conducting ‘irregular classes’, implement a monthly online Aadhaar-based biometric attendance system for the faculty, as is the current practice in Anna University, and to publish the resolutions passed by the Syndicate on the university’s website.

After acquiring official records under the Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005, the organisation had pointed out that physical inspections were carried out in multiple colleges on the same day although they were several kilometres apart. It also said that certain individuals were listed as principals of multiple colleges at the same time.

articles.title: Disinvestment as key economic strategy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Given the fact that privatisation of several PSEs is a long journey, calibrated disinvestment could serve as an interim measure

S even months into 2026-27, the fiscal year has been shaped by global uncertainty, high energy prices and worries over a deficient monsoon. Against this backdrop, disinvestment and asset monetisation have helped in navigating a challenging fiscal year. While receipts were already on course to meet the budget target, the government’s approval of the sale of its share in the IDBI Bank on October 14 makes it likely that the target will be exceeded. For the industry and investors, the receipts are a signal of the government’s continued commitment to reforms and a larger role for the private sector. This year so far, the disinvestment trajectory has progressed well, even before the IDBI stake sale. According to DIPAM data, the Centre mobilised ₹62,124 crore in April-September 2026 through disinvestment and asset monetisation, of which ₹55,757 crore came from disinvestment. These collections had already reached 78% of the full-year budget target of ₹80,000 crore. With the IDBI proceeds, the collections are to head past the target.

This comes at a time when the government looks to diversify its revenue sources amid rising expenditure commitments. Net tax revenue rose by a modest 3.4% in April-August 2026 and non-tax revenue by 3.2%, while capital expenditure was up by over 18%. Overall, the fiscal deficit has already reached 42% of the budgeted levels which implies a tight balance between revenue shortfalls and spending risks.

However, disinvestment should not be seen merely as a tool for meeting fiscal targets. It is a policy choice aimed at unlocking greater value from public assets, widening public ownership, and improving efficiency and governance through greater market discipline. The 2022 LIC IPO which drew in many first-time retail investors and policyholders remains a prime example.

This was precisely the rationale behind the government’s 2021 New Public Sector Enterprise (PSE) Policy which envisages a “bare minimum presence” of PSEs in strategic sectors. Likewise, the National Monetisation Pipeline (NMP) re-engines capital via mature public assets. A target of ₹16.72 lakh crore has been set under NMP 2.0 for FY26-30 after having achieved 90% of its Phase 1 goal.

This year, however, until this month, receipts had come mainly through Offer for Sale (OFS) measures which help to broaden ownership but keep the status quo on an enterprise’s operations. The strategic sale of the IDBI Bank since Air India in 2022 is an encouraging sign. From an industry perspective, the IDBI sale is more than a one-off sale. It is one of the largest Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) deals in India’s financial sector and constitutes as the first step towards a ‘Privatisation 2.0’ framework. More importantly, this framework is premised on being investor-led, professionally managed and time-bound. Two changes would help to turn into a template.

First, the selection criteria for disinvestments of PSEs should move to a demand-based approach instead of being led by the government. It would work better to first gauge interest across a wider pool and prioritise PSEs that draw strong bids at expected valuations, with structured investor feedback flagging procedural and regulatory hurdles early. Second, a rolling three-year privatisation stream, based on investor interest and the government’s strategic priorities, would give investors time for due diligence, which means deeper participation and better price discovery.

Given the fact that privatisation of several PSEs is a long journey, calibrated disinvestment could serve as an interim measure. CII analysis suggests that bringing the government’s stake down to 51% across 95 listed PSEs could fetch about ₹9 lakh crore, with the government remaining the single largest shareholder. PSEs where the government holds 75% or less could be taken up in the first two years, followed by those with higher government holdings. A dedicated body, with a ministerial board, industry experts as advisers and a management team, could steer the process.

To be sure, none of the above makes a case for fiscal complacency. Deficits and public debt tend to rise in uncertain times and stay elevated long after the shock subsides. Staying on the path of fiscal prudence is essential to ensure that the government can continue investing in health and education without crowding out private investment.

Amidst various global headwinds, a healthy progress on disinvestments with more big-ticket sales such as the IDBI will provide the Centre the required cushion to stay on course with fiscal consolidation.
Chandrajit Banerjee is Director General, Confederation of Indian Industry

articles.title: U.S. Fed holds interest rates steady despite surging inflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The 12-member FOMC voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 and 4.00%, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation

The US Federal Reserve on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) held interest rates steady, in line with market expectations, days ahead of crucial midterm elections where surging inflation has been a key issue.

The 12-member Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 and 4.00%, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation, after having hiked for the first time in three years at its previous meeting in September.

“The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee’s two percent goal,” the Fed said in a statement announcing its decision.
Two members of the committee, Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, dissented, calling instead for an immediate 0.25-percentage-point rate hike.
The central bank has missed its long-term two-percent target for inflation for more than five years, with households and businesses battered by sustained price increases.

U.S. President Donald Trump's war on Iran, launched in late February, has sent energy prices skyrocketing and fueled domestic inflation, alongside his wide-ranging tariff policies. Prices have also been driven by an investment boom in artificial intelligence (AI) technology and the build-out of huge data centres to support it. The decision comes six days ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, in which the Democratic Party is seeking to wrest control of both houses of Congress from Mr. Trump's Republicans. Mr. Trump's handling of the economy has been a key issue throughout the campaign, with working-class households across the country struggling to make ends meet despite largely stable overall economic growth.
U.S. consumer inflation came in hotter than expected in September, clocking in at 3.7%, edging back towards a three-year high established in May.
Still, key policymakers at the Fed -- including Mr. Warsh -- have signalled that they did not see an urgency to raise rates again immediately.

Speaking in Bangkok earlier this month, Mr. Warsh said that U.S. economic conditions had “broadly conformed” to policymakers’ expectations, fueling speculation that the Fed may pause at the October meeting.
On Wednesday (October 28, 2026), the Fed said economic activity in the United States was expanding at a “strong” pace, upgrading its language from the FOMC meeting six weeks prior.

Wendy Edelberg, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, told AFP before the meeting that a decision to hold after raising rates in September was potentially contradictory, given the labour market -- the Fed’s other mandate -- has been largely stable.
“In terms of the economics of it, I don’t totally understand the logic,” she said.

articles.title: Pioneering U.S. labour leader Dolores Huerta dies at 96
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Dolores Huerta took the reins of the U.S. farmworker movement in the 1960s with Chavez
Dolores Huerta, the U.S. labour leader and civil rights icon whose union work changed the lives of migrant workers, has died, her family said Wednesday (October 28, 2026). She was 96.

For nearly four decades, Huerta was vice president of United Farm Workers, the union she founded with Cesar Chavez, organising strikes and walkouts that won improvements in working conditions for the millions of men and women who labour in U.S. fields.
"We are deeply saddened to announce that our beloved mother, Dolores Huerta, has passed away today at the age of 96," said a family statement.
"We know that many of you around the world share in our mourning, and we will be following up on plans to recognise and celebrate her incredible life and legacy."
Erik Olvera, a spokesman for her family, told AFP on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) that Huerta died of cancer in the morning surrounded by loved ones.
Born in New Mexico and raised in California, Huerta took the reins of the U.S. farmworker movement in the 1960s with Chavez.
U.S. activists to raise funds to help agitating farmers
At the time, she was raising seven children -- she later had more -- while going through a divorce.
While Huerta was the organising force behind the union, Chavez was its charismatic leader and the public face who became an icon to generations on the left, even after his death in 1993.
But that fame and the seemingly tight relationship between him and Huerta hid a dark secret that came to light this year, when Huerta said she was one of a number of women Chavez had raped.

"The first time... I didn't feel I could say no because he was someone that I admired, my boss and the leader of the movement I had already devoted years of my life to," she said in a statement to the New York Times , which broke the story.
"The second time I was forced, against my will, and in an environment where I felt trapped."

articles.title: What has driven the high Arab turnout in Israel’s elections?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Arab voter turnout is estimated to be nearly 80%, the highest in at least a decade, according to exit polls

Israel’s October 27 legislative elections recorded a massive voter turnout of 77.7%, the highest since 1999. The country’s Arab citizens, who turned up in massive numbers to vote, remained one of the main factors, contributing to the surge.

While the official figures for voter turnout among Israeli Arabs are yet to be released by the Central Elections Committee, exit polls recorded by Channel 12 estimate Arab voter turnout to be nearly 80%. This implies that the voter turnout among Arab citizens in Israel would be the highest in at least a decade.

Global & Diplomatic Brief: What has driven the high Arab turnout in Israel’s elections?. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and proactive engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

Geopolitical Significance: Strengthening strategic partnerships across the Indo-Pacific, Global South, and multilateral forums such as the UN, G20, BRICS, and SCO remains central to India's foreign policy.

articles.title: India must build a holistic care system
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Care is split across multiple Ministries, from women and child development to housing and urban affairs. Each runs valuable programmes, but without a common framework

India’s development story over the past decade has been one of infrastructure: highways, metro lines, electrification and digital public platforms, each treated as a foundation for growth that requires public investment and planning. One foundation on which every household and economy depends has not received the same attention: care.

Everyone needs care at some point in life. How care is organised shapes people’s opportunities, well-being and participation in society and the economy. When services are absent, families, and women most of all, bear the cost in unpaid work, lost earnings, and narrower opportunities.

In the Periodic Labour Force Survey 2025, 44.4% of women outside the labour force cited childcare and homemaking as the main reason for staying out of the labour force. India’s Time Use Survey 2024 found that 41% of women aged 15–59 provided unpaid care, spending an average of 140 minutes a day on it. Expanding access to affordable, quality care services can give women greater freedom to pursue employment, leisure and participation in public life. articles.title: In the crossfire: on India and the Saudi-Houthi conflict
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India must adopt a pro-active position in the Saudi-Houthi conflict

The killing of an Indian national in a Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia’s Dammam airport is a grim reminder of the dangers the kingdom’s Indian community faces as the conflict between Riyadh and Yemen’s Shia militants escalates. Since the fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis resumed in July, at least two Indians have been killed and 14 others wounded. On Thursday, the Houthis claimed that a yacht with 14 Indians was targeted by Saudi forces near Yemen’s Zuqar island in the Red Sea and that rescue operations were under way. As the Houthis, who control parts of Northern Yemen and its entire Red Sea coast, step up attacks on Saudi infrastructure, including oil facilities and airports, Indians, who are the kingdom’s largest expat community, risk getting caught in the crossfire. With flights disrupted, thousands of Indian pilgrims are stranded. India has condemned Houthi attacks, saying that it “stands in solidarity” with Saudi Arabia. With no end in sight to the fighting and a high possibility of Israel and the U.S. resuming their Iran strikes, further violence and instability in West Asia could make India’s choices increasingly difficult.

The Saudi-Houthi conflict dates back to the Houthi takeover of Sana’a, Yemen’s capital, in 2014. A year later, Saudi Arabia began bombing Yemen to drive the Houthis out. But years of Saudi bombing of one of the poorest Arab countries have proved counterproductive; the Houthis consolidated support among the tribes of northern Yemen and built a powerful territorial army and naval force. The Saudi-Houthi ceasefire of 2022 collapsed in July 2026 after Saudi Arabia recklessly bombed Sana’a airport, to prevent an Iranian plane with a Houthi delegation from landing. The Houthis subsequently began attacking Saudi Arabia’s critical infrastructure, and launched a ground offensive against the Saudi-backed forces in Yemen. The Houthi attacks pose the biggest security challenge to Mohammed bin Salman, Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince and the main architect of the war on Yemen, in decades. Massive Saudi air strikes have neither defeated the Houthis nor restored the kingdom’s deterrence. With its wealth, natural resources, infrastructure and tenuous palace politics, the kingdom remains exposed to Houthi missile and drone attacks, with few good options for a way out. India must prepare a contingency plan for worst-case scenarios. Its immediate priority should be to evacuate stranded Indian pilgrims. It should also articulate a stronger position for stability and work with Arab countries and Tehran to push for a diplomatic settlement to the Iran crisis . For peace to prevail in the Persian Gulf, the guns directed at Iran must first fall silent.

articles.title: Falling short: on Marco Rubio’s second visit to India
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Marco Rubio’s second visit to India this year yielded little in terms of results

The United States Secretary of State’s three-day visit to India , his second in five months, came at a significant time in U.S. politics. Marco Rubio’s Mumbai trip this week was just ahead of the U.S. midterm elections , which would mark the midpoint of President Donald Trump’s second term in office — a point at which the incumbent normally begins to focus on legacy, and possible contenders for the next Presidential election (Mr. Rubio is expected to be one), and start to look for possible partners and friendships around the world. In addition, his visit also raised hopes in New Delhi of a reset in bilateral ties, battered by two years of uncertainty over the Trump administration’s actions. This would include positive moves towards concluding the Bilateral Trade Agreement , reassuring India about U.S. sanctions on the import of Russian oil, preparations for upcoming Trump meets with Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the Manila (ASEAN) and Miami (G-20) summits, discussing plans for the Quad Summit (on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit) that India has been trying to host, and setting a date for Mr. Trump’s India visit. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar’s invitation also offered Mr. Rubio an opportunity to meet their UAE counterpart, Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, to discuss the Gulf situation and to restore energy security and connectivity. And finally, Mr. Rubio’s visit to the Jamnagar Reliance refinery, led to speculation of some major deals on energy, possibly offering more discounts as he pitched for India to buy more American and U.S.-licensed Venezuelan oil.

Given all the high expectations, the visit was bound to come up short. The optics of his visit to Mumbai and Jamnagar, but not New Delhi, which was announced by the U.S. Ambassador to India , gave the Opposition fodder to question the real purpose of the visit. Despite Mr. Rubio’s two visits to India and more than six by Mr. Jaishankar to the U.S. since Mr. Trump took office, relations remain on edge, with issues on trade, tariffs, H-1B restrictions and anti-immigrant measures unaddressed. Also, the U.S.’s narrative on Operation Sindoor (2025), growing ties with Pakistan, and the Trump administration’s rhetoric on India’s economy, diaspora and Russian oil trade have added to India’s unhappiness. The two sides did not announce any agreements and Mr. Jaishankar and Mr. Rubio did not hold a joint press address. However, as they did at the U.S. Independence Day’s 250th anniversary celebrations in Delhi in May, they attended the “Freedom 250” event in Mumbai. Mr. Rubio acknowledged that while no two countries would agree on all issues, he said the U.S.-India alignment on core issues of national interest was “extraordinary” . From this point on, Mr. Rubio must walk that talk, with a view to ensuring that India-U.S. ties are able to move on from the difficulties of the last few years.

Jaishankar’s invitation also offered Mr. Rubio an opportunity to meet their UAE counterpart, Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, to discuss the Gulf situation and to restore energy security and connectivity. And finally, Mr. Rubio’s visit to the Jamnagar Reliance refinery, led to speculation of some major deals on energy, possibly offering more discounts as he pitched for India to buy more American and U.S.-licensed Venezuelan oil.
• Given all the high expectations, the visit was bound to come up short. The optics of his visit to Mumbai and Jamnagar, but not New Delhi, which was announced by the U.S. Ambassador to India , gave the Opposition fodder to question the real purpose of the visit. Despite Mr. Rubio’s two visits to India and more than six by Mr. Jaishankar to the U.S. since Mr. Trump took office, relations remain on edge, with issues on trade, tariffs, H-1B restrictions and anti-immigrant measures unaddressed. Also, the U.S.’s narrative on Operation Sindoor (2025), growing ties with Pakistan, and the Trump administration’s rhetoric on India’s economy, diaspora and Russian oil trade have added to India’s unhappiness. The two sides did not announce any agreements and Mr. Jaishankar and Mr. Rubio did not hold a joint press address. However, as they did at the U.S. Independence Day’s 250th anniversary celebrations in Delhi in May, they attended the “Freedom 250” event in Mumbai. Mr. Rubio acknowledged that while no two countries would agree on all issues, he said the U.S.-India alignment on core issues of national interest was “extraordinary” . From this point on, Mr. Rubio must walk that talk, with a view to ensuring that India-U.S. ties are able to move on from the difficulties of the last few years.

articles.title: A Delhi event unveils fault lines in the Dalit-OBC formulation of SP politics
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The brouhaha over Rajkumar Bhati reciting Ambedkar’s vows shows the limits of the SP’s revival of the Lohiate policy of numerical aggregation

In the high-stakes arena of Uttar Pradesh elections, the line between social representation and competitive polarisation is razor-thin. Samajwadi Party (SP) spokesperson Rajkumar Bhati discovered it last week when he faced trolls from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and a reprimand from the party’s top leadership after participating in a Buddhist Dhamma Diksha ceremony in Delhi.

During the annual ceremony, Mr. Bhati, a prominent OBC leader of SP in western U.P., participated in the mass recitation of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s 22 vows. The viral video recorded him explicitly repeating the controversial opening segments of the pledge, which include the statements: “I will not consider Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh as gods, nor will I worship them. I will not consider Rama and Krishna as gods, nor will I worship them.” He was also filmed repeating the vow to refuse any religious rituals performed by Brahmin priests.

The 22 vows, which Ambedkar took with his followers on October 14, 1956, stem from his formulation of Navayana Buddhism. He did not want his followers to transition from one ritualistic or superstitious framework to another. He observed that historically, whenever reform movements emerged within India, they were eventually absorbed back into the dominant Hindu fold as mere sub-sects. He drafted the vows as an explicit checklist to guarantee a complete, irreversible psychological break from the Hindu social order.

A Gurjar by birth, Mr. Bhati organised a massive rally for party president Akhilesh Yadav in March this year. His Dalit push seemed in line with the party’s Lohiate policy of numerical aggregation, uniting everyone outside the so-called upper-caste hegemony to capture state power. Ram Manohar Lohia’s “Socialisto ne bandhi ganth, pichhde paavein sau mein saat ”, referring to roughly 40% OBC and 20% SC vote in the State, still echoes in the air. He also put forward the idea of roti-beti for intermingling of castes. SP founder Mulayam Singh Yadav put the slogan into action by joining hands with Bahujan Samaj Party founder Kanshi Ram in 1993, captured by the popular slogan, ‘ Mile Mulayam-Kanshi Ram, hawa mein ud gaye Jai Shri Ram’ – but the caste barriers remained. Now Mr. Akhilesh seeks to revive Lohia’s logic through his comprehensive PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) formula.

However, his uncles, Ram Gopal Yadav and Shivpal Yadav, reacted to Mr. Bhati’s overtures, reviving Ambedkar’s fears about numerical aggregation. While Mr. Ram Gopal threatened to strip Mr. Bhati of his post in the party, Mr. Shivpal said, “ Hum Ishwarwadi hain .” Political observers feel the Yadav leadership can’t separate its cultural ties to Lord Krishna. A Shiva temple has come up in the Yadav stronghold of Saifai, whose trust is headed by Mr. Akhilesh.

Right-wing elements reminded the SP of their party president’s recent statement that P in PDA also stood for Pandit. Facing an FIR, Mr. Bhati clarified that he repeated the words out of respect for the organisers and Ambedkar, without intending to change his religion. But he also underlined that Ambedkarites would understand the spirit of his stance and respond to his right-wing trolls.

Dalit intellectuals emphasise Ambedkar consistently argued that the Hindu caste structure is not a simple binary of oppressors and oppressed, but a system of graded inequality. Shudras/OBCs, while socially backward compared to upper castes, historically sit higher in the rural socio-economic hierarchy than Dalits.

The Bhati episode mirrors previous political flashpoints, demonstrating that while mainstream parties actively engage in competitive adulation of Ambedkar, their leadership quickly distances itself the moment a politician explicitly recites the radical, anti-scriptural elements of his 22 vows.

In 2022, Rajendra Pal Gautam, a prominent Dalit leader and senior Minister in Arvind Kejriwal’s Delhi Cabinet, took the same vows at the same event and faced similar pressure from the BJP and its parivar ahead of Gujarat polls. Mr. Kejriwal, who was indulging in competitive communalism at the time, succumbed to pressure. Mr. Gautam resigned and subsequently joined the Congress in 2024. Today, he is the All India Congress Committee in-charge for U.P. and is seen as the central leadership’s eyes and ears.

Whether Mr. Bhati is on a similar trajectory and sees a space in an idea-rich, cadre-thin Congress if SP gives in, only time will tell. Rumblings in the INDIA bloc suggest the SP leadership wants Congress to bring in a share of the mature Dalit vote. When Ajay Rai was replaced and the State Congress presidency was split between Mona Misra and Imran Masood, a senior SP insider told this journalist that if the Congress really wants to turn the clock back, instead of focusing on Brahmins and Muslims, it should try to win back 40-plus Dalit voters from Mayawati’s hold. “The rest we will manage,” he said. This is the voter Mr. Bhati was addressing.

Meanwhile, the BJP is finding itself in a bind over allegedly providing cover to its ‘nationalist’ Dalit leader Dushyant Gautam in the Ankita Bhandari case by making him a Governor. Framing it as beti vs Dalit vote narrative, a section of social media influencers who post in favour of the ruling dispensation accuse the BJP of appeasing a Dalit leader without a considerable mass base, which would hurt the party in U.P.

For now, Mr. Akhilesh, who has often cited an incident where a temple was cleaned with ‘Ganga jal’ after his visit, hasn’t taken a stance on Mr. Bhati’s vows. Political observers feel the BJP seeks to appropriate Ambedkar the same way Brahminical scholars appropriated Gautam Buddha as part of the Hindu pantheon, but the Hindutva ecosystem doesn’t want to extend reservation benefits to those who openly negate the presence of Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh, and herein the Opposition sees a vote bank.
