articles.title: Google begins rollout of app marketplaces programme outside the U.S.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The initiative, known as the Registered App Stores programme, allows rival app marketplaces to compete at a higher level on the Android platform
Google announced that eligible app stores outside the U.S. can apply to be part of the company’s programme that allows them to access simplified installation perks.
The initiative, known as the Registered App Stores programme, allows rival app marketplaces to compete at a higher level on the Android platform.
Once an App Store is registered with Google, users will be able to install apps listed on those stores with just one tap. Users will now have a choice beyond Google’s own offering.

It remains to be seen if this measure will translate to profitable results for Google’s rivals, who have complained about anti-competitive measures on Android that favour Google’s app marketplace over others.

Android defined registered app stores as a “third-party app store that registers with Google to access additional platform capabilities, including one-tap installs, while upholding core ecosystem trust, security, and performance standards.”
The programme is the result of multiple antitrust challenges against Google over the way it operates its app marketplace on Android devices.
While rivals want their own app marketplaces to get a fair chance at drawing in users on Android devices, Google has claimed that its restrictions are aimed at maintaining user security and privacy.

However, rival app stores will still have to pay steep prices to be part of the programme. Participation costs start at $10,000 a year, and the programme is only supported on Android devices running the latest versions of Android 17, which means a number of users around the world are walled out.
Google announced the Registered App Stores programme in March, and it is set to launch in December.

articles.title: What is ‘human composting’ — how does it work?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: What should happen to your body after you die? It’s hardly a topic you’d bring up over dinner, but it’s a decision that will eventually need to be made, either by you or by those you leave behind.

In Australia, the choice has traditionally been between burial and cremation. However, concerns about environmental impact, limited cemetery space and the desire for more sustainable alternatives have encouraged interest in other approaches.
These include natural burial, water cremation and shrouded cremation — where no coffin is used.

Now, New South Wales has become the first Australian state to pass legislation allowing another option: “human composting”, technically known as natural organic reduction, and legally termed “terramation”. The process uses microorganisms to transform human remains into a compost-like material.
📢 So-called terramation will become legal in NSW, with several MPs revealing they want their own bodies turned into soil after they die. [image or embed]
The idea of turning a human body into compost might sound unusual, or even unsettling. But how does it actually work? Is it a better alternative to existing methods?
To answer these questions, we first need to understand decomposition and its essential role in nature.
Throughout history, humans have developed rituals to protect, preserve and dress the dead. Some want a quick return to the earth, while others seek to preserve the body.
From ancient burial vessels and elaborate tombs to coffins, shrouds and embalming, these practices reflect cultural and religious beliefs. They also affect how bodies decompose.
Decomposition begins shortly after death. As cells break down, microorganisms already living inside the body, along with those from the surrounding environment, begin breaking down its tissues.

Carrion insects, particularly flies and beetles, can feed on soft tissues remarkably quickly when temperature, moisture and access to the body are favourable. This is nature’s way of recycling organic matter and returning nutrients to the environment.
The body does not simply disappear. But the timescale and extent of its transformation depend on the conditions, processes and materials involved.

articles.title: Alleged Israeli spy company heavily targeted Starlink users, sources say
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Finding ways to track Starlink ‌users has become a cottage industry as governments around the world try to get a grip on the spread of satellite internet terminals

Experts at a digital defense firm recently found that an Israeli ad tech company was heavily targeting users of Starlink’s ‌satellite internet service in a likely effort to spy on them, according to six people familiar with the matter.

Researchers at ​TrendAI, a unit of Tokyo-based cybersecurity company Trend Micro, concluded the Israeli company Discover-Tech was one of the biggest sources of digital ⁠ads shown to users of SpaceX’s Starlink service and that the ads were likely being used to geolocate or otherwise surveil them, according to the six people.

The researchers, who drew on digital advertising data in TrendAI’s telemetry for their conclusions, found that Discover-Tech had become one of the world’s leading bidders for ads aimed at Starlink ‌users and that it was the No. 1 bidder on Starlink traffic in more than 100 countries, including several where Starlink itself was banned or restricted. Bidding refers to the complex auction system by which advertisers secure space inside people’s browsers and apps.
SpaceX ‌did not respond to requests for comment. Discover-Tech and its chief executive did not respond to requests for comment over the past two ‌weeks.

TrendAI ⁠released a report on October 15 about the targeting of Starlink users but did not name Discover-Tech, instead saying the party ⁠responsible was “an ad tech entity” which it called “Shadow-Earth-79.” The six sources said Shadow-Earth-79 is TrendAI’s codename for Discover-Tech.

TrendAI did not directly address questions about why its report did not identify Shadow-Earth-79 by name, saying in a statement that its approach to attribution was aimed at reducing the risk of mistakes and avoiding “hype-driven labels” or “unstable actor names that can mislead defenders, distort ​risk prioritization, and trigger inappropriate response actions.”

Finding ways to track Starlink ‌users has become a cottage industry as governments around the world try to get a grip on the spread of satellite internet terminals. Because they route data through SpaceX-operated satellites rather than nationally regulated telecommunications firms, the terminals can sidestep local internet restrictions, communicate in hostile areas or coordinate action across battlefields. Starlink has become a particularly important resource in Ukraine, whose military relies on the service for frontline communications and directing drone ‌strikes.

In May, Israeli newspaper Haaretz and the website Intelligence Online separately reported that Israeli-owned businesses were pitching clients on ways to identify and ​track Starlink users. Haaretz said exploiting ad data appeared to play a key role in the process.
The same day that TrendAI published its report on Shadow-Earth-79, Canadian cyber watchdog Citizen Lab and New York advertising technology ⁠firm Confiant outed Discover-Tech by name.
Both groups said the Israeli company abused the ad bidding process, which can leak data about internet users back to the bidder.

Over time, bidders can collect that leaked data, collate it and merge it with other information to de-anonymize users, follow them around the web and, in some ‌cases, set them up for targeting with surveillance software.
Citizen Lab and Confiant said the ads had been shown inside dozens of sensitive networks belonging to media organizations, governments and tech firms.

articles.title: Trump drastically loosens oil and gas methane rules
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Mr. Trump is pushing ways of bringing down energy costs ahead of the midterms, amid voter anger over soaring oil costs caused by his war on Iran
U.S. President Donald Trump announced on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) a sweeping rollback of rules that stop oil and gas producers from emitting methane, a greenhouse gas super pollutant.
Mr. Trump made the announcement at a rally in support of Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, who faces a tough battle for a U.S. Senate seat in November 3 midterm elections.
The regulations were put in place by Republican Trump's Democratic predecessor Joe Biden.
"Tonight, I'm officially terminating Biden's expensive and unnecessary methane regulations to save consumers and energy producers $45 billion," Mr. Trump said at the rally in Lubbock, Texas.
To cheers from the crowd, Mr. Trump added that the move would "unlock vast quantities of Texas natural gas." Texas is by far the country's leading fossil-fuel-producing state.
An Environmental Protection Agency statement earlier this month gave the same $45 billion figure in cost savings, without offering a detailed breakdown of the savings.

"Americans must be able to afford to heat their homes in the winter and fill up their car and drive to work," said EPA administrator Lee Zeldin. "They can't do that when the people producing the energy are weighed down by unnecessary burdens."
Mr. Trump is pushing ways of bringing down energy costs ahead of the midterms, amid voter anger over soaring oil costs caused by his war on Iran.
Polls show Republicans could lose control of Congress to the Democrats in next week's vote.

Methane, the main component of natural gas, is the second-largest cause of global warming behind carbon dioxide — responsible for about a third, or 0.5°C, of total planetary heating since the pre-industrial era.
A molecule of methane traps far more heat than carbon dioxide, but persists in the atmosphere for only seven to 12 years, whereas carbon dioxide can last for hundreds of years.

The changes take aim at rules to curb methane emissions from oil and gas operations. Emissions occur at every stage, from extracting gas held underground, to processing, transmission and distribution.

articles.title: Karnataka Council polls: BJP-JD(S) alliance sweeps all four seats
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The biggest upset for the Congress came from Bengaluru Teachers constituency where five-time MLC and former Deputy Chairman Puttanna lost to NDA candidate A.P. Ranganath.

In a setback to the ruling Congress, the BJP-JD(S) alliance won all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats that went to polls on October 23 — two teachers’ and two graduates’ constituencies. Congress earlier held one of the four seats.

The biggest upset for Congress came from Bengaluru Teachers constituency where five-time MLC and former Deputy Chairman Puttanna lost to NDA candidate A.P. Ranganath. BJP candidate Shashil G. Namoshi secured his fifth victory in the North-East Teachers’ constituency, defeating Congress nominee Sharanappa Mattur.

In the West Graduates’ constituency, S.V. Sankanur secured his third consecutive victory , defeating Congress’s Mohan Limbikai. In South East Graduates’ constituency, BJP candidate K.M. Suresha defeated Congress candidate Shashi Hulikuntemutt.

The result has rejuvenated the NDA partners, who were jolted earlier this year after cross-voting of 11 of its MLAs during the poll to seven Legislative Council seats in June. The Congress had won five out of seven seats and the saffron party had won two. Earlier in May, the Congress had also won Davangere South and Bagalkot bypolls , retaining both the seats despite strong internal differences.

The victory is being seen as a result of the co-ordinated effort betwee the BJP and JD(S) that paid off. It has shown that the partners can transfer their support to each other’s candidates. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar acknowledged the defeat and said that they would introspect on it, but insisted that it was no “precursor” to the future elections as interpreted by the NDA partners.
Though the Council election results will not affect the stability of the Congress government, the strong performance of the NDA partners will give the opposition a momentum.

articles.title: SCR rolls out GPS tracking devices for 1,800 patrolmen across three divisions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Railway patrolemn check for loose fish bolts, defects in switches and crossings, damaged fittings on girder bridges and open-top culverts, broken or burnt sleepers, damaged plates and tie bars, and other track-related issues

South Central Railway (SCR), in order to further enhance the safety in train operations , has introduced 1,800 GPS tracker devices to the patrolmen/trackmen covering all the three divisions of Hyderabad, Secunderabad and Nanded.

These devices are intended to assist patrolmen and track maintainers who play a crucial role in ensuring the safe and punctual movement of trains. These frontline railway workers inspect tracks, bridges and other infrastructure round the clock to detect defects and prevent accidents.

Every day and night, patrolmen walk along railway lines and bridges carrying essential equipment while keeping a close watch on track conditions. Depending on the section assigned, they cover distances ranging from three kilometres on single-line routes to six kilometres on double-line routes during each patrol.

Their responsibilities include checking for loose fish bolts, defects in switches and crossings, damaged fittings on girder bridges and open-top culverts, broken or burnt sleepers, damaged plates and tie bars, and other track-related issues. They also monitor water levels and the flow of water near railway infrastructure, particularly during adverse weather conditions, according to senior railway officials.

Whenever a patrolman notices a broken rail, damaged weld, ballast washout, theft of fittings or any other serious defect, he is required to immediately protect the track as per railway safety rules, take preliminary corrective measures wherever possible and alert the nearest Station Master, Permanent Way Inspector and his supervisor.
South Central Railway (SCR) patrolman at work | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT

The GPS-enabled devices will also allow supervisors to monitor patrolmen’s movements in real time. Each tracker, fitted with a SIM card, will be mapped to an individual patrolman and must be carried and switched on while on duty. The system will also alert supervisors if a patrolman deviates from the designated patrol route.

“This device will also help ensure the personal safety of patrolling staff by identifying their exact location. It has three alert buttons to contact immediate supervisors and an ‘SOS’ button for emergencies,” said SCR Chief Public Relations Officer A. Sridhar. The GPS devices will store movement data for up to six months, which can help railway authorities verify ground conditions and investigate any untoward incidents, he added.

articles.title: Supreme Court terms cybercrime as digital dacoity, refuses consolidation of cases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Strongly condemning the organised cybercrime rackets targeting senior citizens through digital arrests, the CJI said those involved must face stringent action

Terming cybercrime as “digital dacoity”, the Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) refused to consolidate over 30 criminal complaints pending against two persons in 12 states for allegedly allowing the use of their company’s account as a mule for the commission of various offences.

“Digital arrests and such cyber offences are digital dacoity… there is no question of giving any judicial forum to such persons,” a Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said.
Strongly condemning the organised cybercrime rackets targeting senior citizens through digital arrests, the CJI said those involved must face stringent action.
“An 81-year-old from Ernakulam (Kerala) was defrauded of ₹1.90 crore and his money was deposited in your mule account,” the CJI said.
“You decided to use the account of your company for cybercrime like digital arrest,” the Bench said while refusing to entertain the plea of Gourab Kumar Saha and Nidhi Bhandari.
The Bench refused to allow the accused to use such proceedings to disrupt investigations in different States.
Justice Bagchi asked as to why victims should be forced to travel to Delhi merely for the convenience of an accused seeking consolidation.

“Your right to seek transfer of cases to a place of your convenience cannot override the right of the victims and the investigating agency… We can consider it if Delhi police say so for the convenience of investigation. We do not take your weight to dilute the investigation across the country,” Justice Bagchi said.

The CJI asked if a victim, whose defrauded money was deposited in Hong Kong and Bangkok, could be asked to go there for redress. The petitioner ultimately withdrew the plea. Thirty-five criminal cases pertaining to cybercrimes are pending against the accused in states including Delhi, Maharashtra, Kerala, Telangana and Gujarat.

articles.title: Supreme Court agrees to hear challenge to definition of ‘industry’ in new Central law
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The All India Trade Union Congress Tamil Nadu’s petition challenged the definition of ‘industry’ under the Industrial Relations Code (IRC) 2020 as “deliciously vague”; The senior counsel Gopal Sankaranarayanan said the definition in the IRC Code did not meet the requirements of the ‘triple test’

The Supreme Court agreed on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) to hear a petition filed by the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) Tamil Nadu challenging the definition of ‘industry’ under the Industrial Relations Code (IRC) 2020 as “deliciously vague”, especially when the new law exempts a wide array of institutions from charitable to sovereign functions of the government.

The IRC affords legal protections to workers who are employed in institutions which come under the ambit of ‘industry’. Section 2(p) of the IRC defines industry as any institution engaged in a “systematic activity carried on by co-operation between an employer and worker for the production, supply or distribution of goods or services with a view to satisfy human wants or wishes”.

Appearing before a Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan and advocate Aarthi Rajan, for the trade union, referred to the exceptions to ‘industry’ listed in the Code.

Mr. Sankaranarayanan submitted that the exceptions to ‘industry’ included institutions wholly or substantially engaged in charitable, social or philanthropic service to “any activity of the appropriate government relatable to sovereign functions” to “any other activity as may be notified by the Central government”.
“Is there a problem with the definition of ‘industry’?” Chief Justice Kant asked.
Editorial | Triple test, adrift: On the ruling on definition of ‘industry’

The senior counsel said the definition in the Code did not meet the requirements of the ‘triple test’. A 1978 seven-judge Constitution Bench judgment, authored by Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer, in the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board v. A. Rajappa case, had laid down conditions that any activity which was systematic or organised, operated on the basis of employer-employee cooperation and dealt in the production of goods and services to satisfy human wants came within the ambit of ‘industry’. The judgment had brought even hospitals, educational institutions and municipalities within the fold of ‘industry’.

In August 2026, a nine-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice Kant had reviewed the interpretation given by Justice Iyer in 1978 to the definition of ‘industry’ under Section 2(j) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. However, the nine-judge Bench had been preceded by the coming into force of the 2020 Code, which largely made the reference to it infructuous.

The majority on the nine-judge Bench in August this year had held that ‘industry’ under Section 2(p) of the Industrial Relations Code (IRC), which came into force in November 2025, would not be “burdened” by the interpretation in the 1978 judgment of Section 2(j) of the 1947 Act.

In his majority opinion, Chief Justice Kant had clarified that the 1978 judgment and its conclusion would not act as the “sheet anchor” or the foundation for any future interpretation of Section 2(p) of the IRC.
“The future of ‘industry’ in Section 2(p) of IRC is not burdened by the interpretation of 2(j) in the Industrial Disputes Act,” Chief Justice Kant had observed in the August 2026 judgment.

In fact, the CJI’s opinion had even suggested a “refinement” of the 1978 triple test. While acknowledging that the core principles of the test had stood the test of time in deciding industrial disputes, the CJI said its elements could have been “articulated differently so that the scope and contours of 2(j) could have been better reflected”. However, the CJI had said this was only a “considered opinion”, and should not be used to displace the governing legal position on pending proceedings or dig up decided cases.

• The Supreme Court agreed on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) to hear a petition filed by the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) Tamil Nadu challenging the definition of ‘industry’ under the Industrial Relations Code (IRC) 2020 as “deliciously vague”, especially when the new law exempts a wide array of institutions from charitable to sovereign functions of the government.

articles.title: Four huts gutted in fire in Navi Mumbai, no casualties
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Household belongings inside the huts and vehicles parked nearby were severely damaged; cause of the fire is being probed
A major fire destroyed four huts at a village in Maharashtra's Navi Mumbai township on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) morning, officials said.
No casualties were reported, they said, adding that household belongings inside the huts and four vehicles were damaged in the fire.
The blaze erupted at 6.15 a.m. in the huts located at Karave village along the Palm Beach Road on the Vashi-Belapur route, a fire official said.
After being alerted, firefighters rushed to the spot and brought the blaze under control by 8 a.m., Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation's Fire Officer Purushottam Jadhav said.

All household belongings inside the huts were destroyed in the fire. A scooter and an electric bike parked nearby were gutted, while a four-wheeler and an auto-rickshaw also suffered severe damage, he said.

articles.title: Netanyahu bloc leads after half of Israeli votes counted but no majority
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: After 51.8% of ballots were counted, Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc was shown to have 55 of the 120 seats in the parliament; partial results suggest that Eisenkot-led Opposition bloc would have enough seats for a majority if there was a coalition agreement with the Arab parties

The camp of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was ahead of his rival's Opposition bloc but still short of a majority on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) after 50% of votes were counted in Israel's pivotal general election.

Voters turned out in the highest numbers in decades to give their verdict on Mr. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister who has pushed the country sharply to the right and unleashed a wave of wars in response to Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack.
Following the vote, both Mr. Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot vowed to form a government despite neither being projected to win a majority.
After 51.8% of ballots were counted, Mr. Netanyahu's bloc was shown to have 55 of the 120 seats in the parliament.
Mr. Eisenkot's Opposition bloc had 49 seats and the Arab parties 16. The partial results are likely to change as more votes are counted.

Exit polls had shown that Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief and political novice, and his Opposition bloc were neck-and-neck with Mr. Netanyahu's hard-right camp, with both winning about 51 seats, well away from the threshold for a majority in parliament.

The strongest gains came from Arab Israeli parties whose voters turned out in soaring numbers against Netanyahu, who has relentlessly warned that the minority would dilute the Jewish nationalist direction in which he has taken Israel.
The partial results suggest that Mr. Eisenkot's bloc would have enough seats for a majority if there was a coalition agreement with the Arab parties.

But Mr. Eisenkot said during the campaign he would not govern with Israeli Arab lawmakers, echoing the position of Mr. Netanyahu, who has suggested a government relying on Arab votes would lack legitimacy.
Arab lawmakers could also give Mr. Eisenkot support in parliamentary votes to maintain a minority government without joining a coalition.

A lack of clear majority for either camp could mean weeks spent trying to cobble together coalitions, with possible new elections on the horizon if negotiations fail. A stalemate could in the immediate term benefit Mr. Netanyahu, who would remain caretaker prime minister until a new government is formed.
Full results are expected by Thursday evening or Friday morning (October 29-30).

articles.title: Iran hasn't tried to repair nuclear facilities damaged in Israeli-U.S. strikes: IAEA chief
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: During a UN Security Council meeting, Rafael Grossi urged Iran to give inspectors access to all nuclear sites, including those damaged in the military attacks; Iran maintains that its nuclear program is peaceful

The head of the UN nuclear agency said on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) there has been no indication Iran has tried to repair or reconstruct its nuclear facilities damaged in U.S. and Israeli military strikes this year or last year.

President Donald Trump has said one of the major reasons the U.S. went to war with Iran on Feb. 28 was to deny Tehran the ability to develop nuclear weapons, even as he has insisted that strikes the U.S. carried out on Iranian nuclear sites in June 2025 “obliterated” the country's atomic program.

During a UN Security Council meeting, International Atomic Energy Agency chief Rafael Grossi urged Iran to give inspectors access to all nuclear sites, including those damaged in the military attacks. The IAEA has not been able to verify the status of Iran's stockpile of near weapons-grade uranium since the U.S. bombed its sites last year.
However, Mr. Grossi said that “since June 2025, we have not identified any activity to repair or reconstruct any of the facilities damaged in the military attacks of 2025 and 2026."

Mr. Trump has consistently downplayed the economic impact of the Iran war, which has emerged as a liability for Republicans heading into next week's midterm elections, and has argued that higher fuel prices are worth paying to prevent a nuclear-armed Iran.
The White House didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on Mr. Grossi's remarks.

Iran maintains that its nuclear program is peaceful. However, the IAEA says the country has a stockpile of 440.9 kilograms (972 pounds) of uranium enriched up to 60% purity — a short, technical step away from weapons-grade levels of 90%.

The UN meeting on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) was called by Bahrain, Denmark, Latvia, France, the United Kingdom and United States after the IAEA referred Iran to the Security Council for failing to comply with its nuclear nonproliferation obligations. Russia and China, allies of Iran, tried unsuccessfully to prevent the meeting.

Under those obligations, which are part of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, Iran is legally bound to declare all nuclear material and activities and allow IAEA inspectors to verify that none of it is being diverted from peaceful uses.

Iran's UN deputy ambassador Gholamhossein Darzi attacked the council for its silence after the U.S.-Israeli attacks, denouncing their “wars of aggression against Iran” and accusing the U.S. of committing war crimes against the Iranian people.

He never mentioned the IAEA's unanswered questions or the demand to return its inspectors. Instead, he asserted that “Israel possesses nuclear weapons, yet your concern is the absence of inspectors in Iran.” Israel has never confirmed that it possesses nuclear weapons.
US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz called Iran a “brutal dictatorship” and asked if the Iranian ambassador wanted to apologize to Bahrain's envoy, a council member, for attacking his country.

1. Core Context & Background: During a UN Security Council meeting, Rafael Grossi urged Iran to give inspectors access to all nuclear sites, including those damaged in the military attacks; Iran maintains that its nuclear program is peaceful

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The head of the UN nuclear agency said on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) there has been no indication Iran has tried to repair or reconstruct its nuclear facilities damaged in U.S. and Israeli military strikes this year or last year.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz called Iran a “brutal dictatorship” and asked if the Iranian ambassador wanted to apologize to Bahrain's envoy, a council member, for attacking his country.

articles.title: Hegseth proposes 'ambitious' U.S.-ASEAN defence framework at Philippine summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The United States has been seeking to boost its regional defence partnerships in recent years, citing the need to uphold what it terms a "free and open Indo-Pacific" as China has increasingly flexed its muscles in the region

U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth proposed the creation of an "ambitious" new U.S.-ASEAN defence framework on Wednesday (October 28, 2026), telling the bloc's leaders it could help them navigate "critically important" years ahead.

The United States has been seeking to boost its regional defence partnerships in recent years, citing the need to uphold what it terms a "free and open Indo-Pacific" as China has increasingly flexed its muscles in the region.
Mr. Hegseth, speaking before a meeting with defence chiefs from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations in Cebu, praised what he called the region's "pragmatism" and "proud nationalism".
"We're not going to agree on everything, nor do we need to," he said, calling for cooperation where shared interests overlap.

"As we look to the future in this region, I'd like us to be even more ambitious... we propose that we work together to develop a U.S.-ASEAN Framework for Defence Cooperation," Mr. Hegseth said, without offering details.
"A practical framework that guides our cooperation over the next several years. I will note a critically important next several years."
He added that the United States was ready to begin the project as Singapore assumes the chairmanship of the ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting (ADMM)-Plus in the coming year.
The grouping includes not only the bloc's 11 member states but representatives from the United States, Japan, China, Australia and others.
Mr. Hegseth also called for the strengthening of "maritime domain awareness" and advanced cooperation among naval forces.

"These are not symbolic things; they are concrete demonstrations of what serious partners do, serious partners train together, learn together, plan together, and build the confidence and competence necessary to prevent conflict," he said.
U.S. ally, the Philippines, has been engaged in years of confrontations with China over disputed areas of the South China Sea.
China's military and coast guard presence in contested areas of the critical waterway nearly doubled in September, Manila said this month.

articles.title: Can Indian homegrown smartphone brands compete with global giants?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The government’s goal of establishing a homegrown smartphone brand by October 2028 sets a clear benchmark for national ambition. However, achieving market relevance against global leaders requires moving past price competition and contract assembly

India’s IT Minister, Ashwini Vaishnaw , in a recent interaction with NDTV , outlined an ambitious target that by October 23, 2028, India will have its own mobile phone brand, designed and made locally. While the minister’s intent reflects a strong government policy to foster indigenous manufacturing and self-reliance, translating that vision into commercial success presents steep operational and market hurdles.

The competitive landscape is daunting as Chinese Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) control nearly 70% of India’s smartphone market, as per Counterpoint. Apple, on the other side of the globe, dominates premium market phones . The iPhone maker’s dominance has forced Chinese players to re-evaluate their strategies across price bands.

Ai+, a relatively new domestic smartphone maker, shipped over 10 lakh units in the September ending quarter. And newer entrants like Mivi and Boltt are entering the market at time when the collective market share of India-made smartphones is a modest 7%, per Counterpoint analysis.
But can these brands compete against Apple, Nothing, Samsung, Oppo and Vivo?

Evaluating the 2028 timeline requires a close examination of how Indian smartphone brands have historically performed. For years, domestic players have played catch up with global handset brands instead of driving true innovation — a strategy that has left local firms vulnerable to rapid market shifts.
Domestic manufacturers must need a fundamental shift in their strategy, Faisal Kawoosa, founder of Techarc, said.
“We will have to change our approach to achieving this,” he noted, highlighting two major flaws in the traditional catch-up model.

“First, we have to be subservient to the global supply chain, and our mission’s success depends on how well it serves their business goals,” he explained. “The second challenge is that, since we decide to do our version of something that already exists, by the time we get there, market conditions may have changed, and whatever we achieve might lose relevance. For example, if we focus on, say, the sub-$200 market, customer preferences might shift strongly toward upper tiers, as is happening now.”

Achieving true brand independence demands comprehensive R&D across hardware, software, materials, and apps. Mr. Kawoosa said this foundation cannot be built hastily. “We have to do intensive, broad R&D that also covers materials, electronics, software, hardware, apps, etc. We can’t achieve this in 2 years; it will take at least 5-10 years, provided we do it sincerely,” he stated.
He added that India’s product design capabilities are not yet ready to propose disruptive solutions that attract global supply chains, questioning long-term sustainability by 2028.

Beyond R&D timelines, market dynamics present an equally steep challenge as the Indian smartphone market is a zero-sum game where one brand’s gain is another’s loss, according to Tarun Pathak, Research Director at Counterpoint. To achieve meaningful scale, brands must progress through clear operational stages.

“Go-to-market, channel and pricing can help a brand reach 0-5% share, even with an ODM-dependent supply chain,” Mr. Pathak explained. “Getting to 5-10% requires real hardware differentiation, design and R&D, local sourcing, and solid operations: brand building, after-sales and channel execution. Anything above 10% requires massive scale, software differentiation, strong brand pull and tight control over hardware.”

Can Indian homegrown smartphone brands compete with global giants?

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports

The government’s goal of establishing a homegrown smartphone brand by October 2028 sets a clear benchmark for national ambition. However, achieving market relevance against global leaders requires moving past price competition and contract assembly

India’s IT Minister, Ashwini Vaishnaw , in a recent interaction with NDTV , outlined an ambitious target that by October 23, 2028, India will have its own mobile phone brand, designed and made locally. While the minister’s intent reflects a strong government policy to foster indigenous manufacturing and self-reliance, translating that vision into commercial success presents steep operational and market hurdles.

The competitive landscape is daunting as Chinese Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) control nearly 70% of India’s smartphone market, as per Counterpoint. Apple, on the other side of the globe, dominates premium market phones . The iPhone maker’s dominance has forced Chinese players to re-evaluate their strategies across price bands.

Ai+, a relatively new domestic smartphone maker, shipped over 10 lakh units in the September ending quarter. And newer entrants like Mivi and Boltt are entering the market at time when the collective market share of India-made smartphones is a modest 7%, per Counterpoint analysis.

But can these brands compete against Apple, Nothing, Samsung, Oppo and Vivo?

Evaluating the 2028 timeline requires a close examination of how Indian smartphone brands have historically performed. For years, domestic players have played catch up with global handset brands instead of driving true innovation — a strategy that has left local firms vulnerable to rapid market shifts.

Domestic manufacturers must need a fundamental shift in their strategy, Faisal Kawoosa, founder of Techarc, said.

“We will have to change our approach to achieving this,” he noted, highlighting two major flaws in the traditional catch-up model.

“First, we have to be subservient to the global supply chain, and our mission’s success depends on how well it serves their business goals,” he explained. “The second challenge is that, since we decide to do our version of something that already exists, by the time we get there, market conditions may have changed, and whatever we achieve might lose relevance. For example, if we focus on, say, the sub-$200 market, customer preferences might shift strongly toward upper tiers, as is happening now.”

Achieving true brand independence demands comprehensive R&D across hardware, software, materials, and apps. Mr. Kawoosa said this foundation cannot be built hastily. “We have to do intensive, broad R&D that also covers materials, electronics, software, hardware, apps, etc. We can’t achieve this in 2 years; it will take at least 5-10 years, provided we do it sincerely,” he stated.

He added that India’s product design capabilities are not yet ready to propose disruptive solutions that attract global supply chains, questioning long-term sustainability by 2028.

Beyond R&D timelines, market dynamics present an equally steep challenge as the Indian smartphone market is a zero-sum game where one brand’s gain is another’s loss, according to Tarun Pathak, Research Director at Counterpoint. To achieve meaningful scale, brands must progress through clear operational stages.

“Go-to-market, channel and pricing can help a brand reach 0-5% share, even with an ODM-dependent supply chain,” Mr. Pathak explained. “Getting to 5-10% requires real hardware differentiation, design and R&D, local sourcing, and solid operations: brand building, after-sales and channel execution. 3. articles.title: Apple says a small number of iPhone Duo inner display impacted
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: iPhone Duo challenges Samsung’s foldables across the world, while competing with Google, Huawei, Vivo and Motorola in global market

After some customers who bought Apple’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo , reported that the device’s inner screen cracked, the Cupertino-based tech giant has said it is “aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units.”

Responding to The Hindu’s query, Apple said, “If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement.” However, no such incident has been reported in India.

“The response to iPhone Duo from early users has been incredibly positive, and we are seeing exciting things from developers who are rapidly updating their apps to take advantage of its unique form factor,” Apple said.
Mark Gurman, Bloomberg’s tech editor, also pointed out in his report that iPhone Duo users are sending him images and stories of their $2,000 device breaking within hours.
iPhone Duo challenges Samsung’s foldables across the world, while competing with Google, Huawei, Vivo and Motorola in global markets.
Launched alongside iPhone 18 Pro series, the iPhone Duo comes with a passport-style form factor, having a 5.4 inch cover display, and a 7.6 inch main OLED display.
It runs on A20 Pro processor and sports a 48 MP main camera and a 48 MP ultrawide lens. It uses a 12 MP front camera on cover and an under-display FaceTime camera on the main screen.
iPhone Duo costs ₹2,99,900 in India, and went on sale starting October 23.
Some social media posts have called the images of a broken Duo display as AI-generated. We could not verify those claims.

articles.title: What happens inside the brain during a stroke?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The first few hours of a stroke determine how damaged the brain can become. Knowing the signs and seeking timely medical help is crucial

A stroke is an urgent situation where either the flow of blood to the brain is cut off, or there is a rupture of the blood vessels in the brain. Oxygen and glucose are the two elements essential for brain activity. Interruption of their supply results in impairment of brain activity and eventual damage of brain tissues -- and this damage occurs in minutes. The first few hours of a stroke, therefore, determine how damaged the brain can become.

Strokes can be categorised into ischemic strokes and haemorrhagic strokes. In ischemic strokes, the stroke occurs due to the blocking of an artery by a blood clot. In haemorrhagic strokes, there is a rupture of the blood vessel, which leads to blood in the brain tissue. Regardless of the type of stroke, the result is damage to the brain tissue, which can result in vital body functions including speaking, movement, vision, memory and coordination becoming impaired.

An ischemic stroke is accompanied by oxygen starvation of the affected brain tissue. Due to insufficient energy resources, brain cells cannot function normally. The chemical composition of the brain cells, therefore, changes, which results in the accumulation of toxic substances that harm brain cells and other structures. With continued oxygen starvation, cells continue to deteriorate. The damage, however, does not occur uniformly. In the central area of the brain (core) where oxygen starvation is critical, damage can occur rapidly and irreversibly. Around this area, there is a zone called the ischemic penumbra. Here, even if blood flow is low, brain cells can survive for a certain period of time. They can be saved if blood flow is restored promptly.

The effect of bleeding in a haemorrhagic stroke is brought about by the leaking of blood into the brain when there is a rupture of a blood vessel. This may lead to injury of brain cells, and also interfere with proper blood and cerebral spinal fluid flow in the brain.

There are only so many minutes that the brain can withstand interrupted blood flow. Brain cells (neurons) begins to undergo irreversible damage within 3 to 5 minutes of interrupted blood flow. With each minute that goes by, 1.9 million neurons, i.e. 32 neurons per second, die due to lack of oxygenation, which is why we emphasise that ‘time is brain’. The first few hours are critical since at this point, one needs to assess what kind of stroke it is and start appropriate treatment.

In some cases of ischemic stroke, intravenous thrombolysis, the administration of drugs that dissolve the clot within the blood vessels, might be given in the first 4.5 hours after symptoms develop. In some patients with large vessel blockage, there might be indications for mechanical thrombectomy. In simple terms, a mechanical thrombectomy involves the removal of the clot using special equipment, and it might be done up to 24 hours after the patient was last seen without symptoms. In cases of haemorrhagic strokes, others strategies must be employed: this includes blood pressure control, correction of the consequences of taking blood thinners, management of intracranial pressure, and surgical procedures, where necessary.

Not all patients automatically qualify for all interventions. There are other issues that have to be taken into account, including the patient’s medical status, imaging studies, timing of stroke symptoms, and dangers involved in the therapy. Even some of those who come after these time windows, can still be eligible for certain treatment procedures after imaging is done.

The effects of a stroke vary, depending on the site and degree of damage within the brain. Movement centres can be damaged leading to weakness or paralysis that usually affects one side of the body. Speech centres could be damaged causing speech problems and comprehension difficulties or trouble reading and writing. A stroke involving the visual pathways leads to a sudden loss of vision or partial visual fields. If the cerebellum or the brainstem is involved, there could be a problem with dizziness, poor coordination, problems swallowing, double vision or loss of balance. There could also be memory, attention and decision-making problems and problems with emotional regulation.
It is important to know and understand these symptoms since sometimes a stroke occurs without the characteristic facial drooping or arm weakness of the disease.
The BE FAST method is an effective means of identifying the symptoms of a stroke

Sudden changes in vision, lack of balance, confusion or even a severe headache without apparent reason might be symptoms of a stroke as well. Disappearing symptoms within a minute or two shouldn’t be considered harmless and require immediate medical examination.

The ‘golden hour’ is significant to preserve as much of brain function as possible and to ensure best possible outcomes, but this does not mean medical professionals cease working after this window is over. Medical teams will continue monitoring the condition of the patient, controlling blood pressure and preventing additional harm to him or her. In case the condition of the patient becomes satisfactory, it is likely that he or she will be offered physiotherapy, speech and language therapy, occupational therapy and cognitive therapy.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Environment Minister’s remark on soap, shampoo use causing Noyyal River foaming draws ire
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: After a controversy erupted, the Minister, speaking to the media in Chennai on Wednesday, emphasised that the combination of surfactants, detergents, and phosphorus was responsible for excessive foaming, not industrial effluents

A comment by Tamil Nadu Minister for Environment and Climate Change V.K. Rajeev, that soap and shampoo used by the public can also cause excessive foaming in the Noyyal River, which flows through Tiruppur district, has sparked criticism.

Speaking to mediapersons after an inspection of the river on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), the Minister made this statement while warning dyeing and textile units of strict action if they released untreated effluents into the river, taking advantage of the copious flow of rainwater during the Northeast monsoon season.

After a controversy erupted over his statement, the Minister, speaking to the media in Chennai on Wednesday (October 28), emphasised that the combination of surfactants, detergents, and phosphorus was responsible for excessive foaming of waterbodies, not industrial effluents. The State government had been taking all measures to ensure that people were not affected by hazardous waste, he added.

He said complaints were being examined and addressed promptly. Recently, the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board (TNPCB) inspected Vaniyambadi and found that the foaming was caused by surfactants and not industrial effluents.
Environmental activists and farmers have, for long, been complaining about foaming in the Noyyal River throughout the year. The TNPCB will issue a statement on the issue, official sources said.

Reacting to the Minister’s statement, Pattali Makkal Katchi (PMK) president Anbumani Ramadoss criticised Mr. Rajiv on Wednesday, saying that “even children know that the foaming of rivers such as the Noyyal is caused by the discharge of wastes into them.” He demanded concrete action to protect rivers.

“The uncontrolled discharge of textile dyeing effluents into the Noyyal River in Coimbatore, Tiruppur, and Karur districts is the reason for the excessive foaming. It is also widely known that the contamination of the Orathuppalayam Dam, built across the Noyyal River, with textile dyeing effluents has prompted farmers to protest against the opening of the dam,” he said.

The excessive foaming at the Kelavarapalli Dam on the Thenpennai River is caused by the discharge of waste into the river in Karnataka, he said, adding that he had personally inspected both rivers on several occasions and urged the authorities to take action to prevent the discharge of effluents into them. The Supreme Court, too, has issued several orders to the governments of Tamil Nadu and Karnataka in this regard, he said.

He further pointed out that the Minister had praised the functioning of the textile dyeing effluent treatment facilities in the district while assuring dyeing mill owners that steps would be taken to fulfil their demands. “This raises serious doubts about whose interests the Minister is representing and whose voice he is echoing,” Dr. Anbumani said.

articles.title: Cyclone ‘Arnab’: Flash flood alert for several southern Odisha districts amid heavy rain
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Around 28,000 people had been evacuated across eight districts so far, against a planned evacuation target of 48,000, as per Odisha Special Relief Commissioner
Amid heavy rainfall, several districts in southern Odisha on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) are bracing for possible flash floods as cyclone ‘Arnab’ trudged past Andra Pradesh coast
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued flash flood alerts for Koraput, Nabarangpur, Rayagada, Gajapati, Kalahandi, Nuapada, Balangir, Kandhamal and Ganjam districts.

According to the IMD, Mahendragarh in Gajapati district recorded the highest rainfall at 25 cm, followed by Pottangi in Koraput district at 19 cm. Mohana, another location in Gajapati recorded 17 cm, while parts of Ganjam district received 16 cm and Chhatrapur recorded 15 cm.
Uprooting of trees, landslides and inundation of low-lying areas were reported from different districts.

“Rainfall is likely to increase further. We expect heavy rain in Malkangiri, Koraput, Nuapada and Kalahandi districts. Keeping this forecast in mind, we have deployed disaster response teams in accordance with our preparedness plans,” State Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh Pravakar Patil said on Wednesday (October 28, 2026).

“Response teams and fire services personnel are in place, along with Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force and National Disaster Response Force teams. Collectors in all the districts are on alert,” Mr. Patil said.

He said around 28,000 people had been evacuated across eight districts so far, against a planned evacuation target of 48,000. As many as 2,200 pregnant women had been shifted to different health institutions. Around 200 pregnant women had delivered in Ganjam district.

“The situation remains under control, and no untoward incident has been reported so far. Geographically, Gajapati district is close to the area in Andhra Pradesh where the cyclone made landfall. We are also keeping a close watch on the situation, as the district has received heavy rainfall,” the SRC said.

Mr. Patil also cautioned that the cyclone’s movement towards Chhattisgarh could bring heavy rainfall over the next 24 hours. “If it has any impact on the Mahanadi river system, we will need to address the situation accordingly,” he said.

articles.title: How five women from a Palakkad bakery found YouTube stardom
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: VillageFoodKerala, a YouTube channel featuring five women cooking traditional dishes, taps into the appeal of long forgotten recipes and rustic charm of village life

A lively bunch of women, dressed in identical blue saris, is busy preparing a Deepavali special “bread sweet” for the camera. Using just ghee, bread, milk and sugar, they whip up a dish that looks easy and delicious. Meet the women from VillageFoodKerala, a YouTube channel documenting recipes, rustic flavours and traditional cooking styles of Palakkad.

Since the launch of the channel on YouTube and Facebook in 2024, VillageFoodKerala has struck a chord with Malayalis the world over, with its nadan (traditional) recipes cooked outdoors in picturesque locations.
Team VillagefoodKerala | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

They shared their dream with the owner of the bakery, Jayaprasad MR, who readily offered to help. He brought on board videographer Karthik S to help with the content, filming and editing and thus began a journey through social media that took people through the joys of simple meals, cooked with love.

The initial days were filled with excitement. “We would sit together and plan what to cook and how to go about it. While shooting, we spent hours outdoors in the scorching heat of Palakkad. But it was an exhilarating experience,” says Sarada.

The journey has also been empowering for these women. “From the confines of the kitchen to facing a camera and speaking confidently, we have come a long way. Now people recognise us. We have become minor celebrities,” laughs Sarada. “When we started out, we were not so sure of ourselves. We are regular working women; we have not had much exposure. But as we kept doing our videos, we discovered so much about ourselves. It gave us a platform to showcase our skills,” she adds. “It fills us with joy when we see people appreciate our content and encourage us.”

The women choose traditional recipes and try to use locally-available ingredients to cook. “Most of the dishes we cook are recipes that have been part of Palakkad’s culinary heritage. We have each gleaned our cooking styles and techniques from our mothers and grandmothers,” says Rajani.
VillagefoodKerala team with Jayaprasad MR and Karthik S with YouTube’s Silver Play Button (in white) | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

The chicken and kumbalanga (ash gourd) curry, for instance, is unique to Palakkad. A spicy curry, the ingredients — chunks of ash gourd and chicken — and masalas are mixed by hand before it is cooked. “That helps in blending the masala well. The ash gourd is believed to balance the heat from the chicken,” adds Rajani.

Some of their other popular recipes include Palakkad style Rawther biryani, moringa leaf pulincurry, Kerala mutton soup, starfruit and sardine curry, raw banana and milk shark curry, papaya and chicken curry and taro stem and tapioca curry. Snacks, cakes and desserts are also part of their videos. “We pick easy-to-make dishes that do not need expensive ingredients, are healthy and use locally-sourced produce,” says Renjini.
Dhanya adds, “We enjoy the process of cooking. We talk, crack jokes, all in our quintessential Palakkad dialect, which we are told, adds to the charm of the content.”

The women are still employed at the bakery and they work on their videos as and when they find time. “We try to do at least four videos a month, but it depends on their work schedule,” says Karthik, who ensures that he adds a cinematic touch, shooting in scenic spots that showcase the beauty of Palakkad. “It was his suggestion that we wear identical saris and that has worked well,” says Jayaprabha.

articles.title: A new ore-der: Can India’s Mineral Exchanges fix the price game?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: India’s proposed mineral exchanges aim to fix price transparency, boost liquidity, and create credible domestic benchmarks for ores like iron ore and beyond

In less than 14 months, an idea to bring India’s fragmented market onto a common electronic platform germinated from legislative intent to a formal regulatory framework and, finally, setting the stage for establishing mineral exchanges.
The proposed exchanges cobbled an ambitious plan, ensuring a transparent marketplace where representative prices reflect demand and supply rather than relying on fragmented negotiations and auctions.
India’s mining sector has historically faced challenges on price transparency, fragmented markets and information asymmetry.

Seeking to effectively address the issues in the sector in a holistic way, the latest institutional reforms may result in the enhanced industrial competitiveness, investment flows and supply-chain resilience.
The proposed exchange framework will spell out how miners sell output, how manufacturers procure raw materials and how India establishes credible domestic reference prices for industrial minerals.

The move comes at a time when minerals are fast turning crucial to the country’s economic security and also when India is increasingly focusing on infrastructure, renewable energy, electric vehicles, defence equipment, advanced manufacturing and clean energy.

Power trading solutions provider PTC India this week said its board has approved incorporation of a wholly-owned subsidiary with an investment of ₹65 crore to set up and operate a mineral exchange. MCXI (Multi Commodity Exchange of India) has established MCX Mineral Exchange of India Limited as a wholly owned subsidiary.
Opinion | Mining in India equals selling the family gold

The amendments to the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act provided the legal bedrock for the exchange, paving way for coal exchanges, marking a paradigm shift in marketing by moving from the traditional “one-to-many” sales model to a competitive “many-to-many” trading platform.
Section 18B of the MMDR Act provides for promoting markets, including trading of minerals through mineral exchanges.

The Ministry of Mines subsequently framed the Mineral Exchange Rules, 2026. The regulatory responsibility will rest with the Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM) under the Ministry of Mines. The government has designated IBM as the authority to register and regulate mineral exchanges for minerals other than coal, lignite and atomic minerals.
Small and medium miners often have limited bargaining power when compared with large buyers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Small and medium miners often have limited bargaining power when compared with large buyers.

articles.title: Live streaming of case mentioning in CJI's court closed
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Disapproving of lawyers making mentions without a comprehensible issue, the CJI had called it "the biggest nuisance" and said the practice "should stop completely"
The Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) closed live streaming of case mentioning in the Court of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant.
Mentioning in the Supreme Court is a procedural mechanism where lawyers or parties-in-person orally or in writing request the CJI or a bench for an urgent hearing or early listing of a case.
The development follows the CJI expressing displeasure on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) after a lawyer mentioned a matter related to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi.
Disapproving of lawyers making mentions without a comprehensible issue, the CJI had called it "the biggest nuisance" and said the practice "should stop completely".
The top court also issued a circular stating that no senior lawyer shall be permitted to make oral mentioning before any court with effect from November 2.
"All concerned are hereby informed that young and junior counsels may, instead, be encouraged to make oral mentioning before the Courts," the circular said.

articles.title: On the question of KIIFB’s future
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: An expert panel constituted by Keralam’s UDF government to review the functioning of KIIFB has recommended winding it up and absorbing its functions into the State government, prompting a closer look at the merits of off-budget borrowings by States and the need to boost public investment in Keralam

In July, Keralam’s newly elected UDF government set up an expert panel to review the functioning of Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB). The panel, headed by a former civil servant, was tasked with recommending measures to restructure KIIFB and strengthen the government’s institutional capabilities, among other things. The committee has recently submitted its report, which has been tabled in the State Assembly.

Apparently critical of KIIFB’s functioning, the committee has recommended winding it up; absorbing its functions and capabilities into the State government, news reports say. The principal reason for the panel’s recommendation is that with the clubbing of KIIFB’s borrowing function with the State budget, the special purpose vehicle (SPV) has lost its primary purpose.

KIIFB, restructured by the LDF government, reportedly boosted the State’s infrastructure investment by raising extra-budgetary resources, including securing soft loans known as “Masala Bonds” from international agencies after the disastrous floods of 2019. However, the SPV’s functioning and financial performance have remained contentious. The comptroller and auditor general’s (CAG) strictures against KIIFB have become a convenient beating stick for the Centre and the Opposition parties in the State. Leftist critics have branded it as the arm of “the Left Managerial State” for promoting controversial projects, bypassing legislative approvals. In the fog of the debate, KIIFB’s original purpose and economic principles underlying it seem to have been lost sight of. We seek to explain them, intending to shed some light on the contentious issue.

Though Keralam has sound traditional transport infrastructure such as road network and rail connectivity, it lags behind in modern facilities, such as high-speed railways or highways, especially when compared to the neighbouring States. Keralam reportedly spends a mere 1.5 per cent of the Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) on infrastructure. This was so in spite of Keralam’s own-tax revenue to GSDP ratio being among the highest among major States, as per the RBI data.

KIIFB was set up in 1999 and underwent a major restructuring in 2016; the institution’s record in expanding public goods is apparently well acknowledged. However, its functioning raised many queries. The CAG found that the SPV’s finances flouted its procedural audits, which became a sticking point between the Centre and the State. Moreover, as KIIFB functioned outside the purview of the State budget, without generating financial profits from its lending, its borrowings being serviced out of the State’s revenue became the heart of the contention.

In the good/bad old days of “planning”, State finances broadly followed the “gap-filling” approach; meaning the Centre made up the difference between a State’s projected revenue growth and its “developmental needs” as per the State plans. It was a negotiated process, part financial and part political. Evidence shows that richer and politically influential States got the lion’s share of the divisible pool of the plan resources.

The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBM) 2003 changed that by seemingly imposing a “hard budget constraint”, with the fiscal deficit capped at 3 per cent of GSDP. The RBI now monitors the size of the State debt. The coupon (interest) rate of the State loans depends on the State’s debt sustainability measures. The hard budget constraint has reportedly improved State finances, or at a minimum, made them transparent.

However, most States have devised a variety of means for securing extra-budgetary resources, or off-budget borrowings (OBBs) – as evident from the RBI’s compilation of State finances. The CAG, tracking OBBs, finds that there is a bewildering variety of them. And the actual OBBs are far higher than what it is able to count, as per its own findings. In other words, ensuring fiscal discipline seems like a cat-and-mouse game between the Centre and States. Incidentally, Keralam is not among the worst offenders.

Globally, a variety of financial institutions and fiscal arrangements have existed outside of the budgetary process. Numerous kinds of para-statal organisations are a feature – not a bug – of the fiscal landscape, especially among fast-growing Asian economies. China, for instance, has a bewildering variety of financial arrangements that enable provinces to draw resources from the national development banks to sustain employment at the local level, augment production and exports and ensure political stability. No wonder, China’s public debt to GDP ratio is nearly 300 per cent – though most of it domestic.

Then, realistically, what should be the rules for managing extra-budgetary resources and institutions for Keralam? Simply speaking, if extra-budgetary resources are productively used and they comply with the government expenditure principles, having such off-budget institutions/borrowings may not be undesirable. This follows the Domar rule: so long as the output growth rate exceeds the interest rate on such loans (either at current or at constant prices), they are being used productively. Since such investments have a public good character, individual projects may not be yielding adequate revenue or covering the full costs. However, if in the aggregate they contribute to growth in state output (GSDP) and follow the Domar rule, then such investments are in principle viable.

However, if the State-level SPVs borrow from external sources for social purposes or green financing, which usually have lower interest rates for longer maturities, they need to be assessed differently, as they involve exchange rate risk. Given Keralam’s fragile ecology and need for substantial low-cost resources for protecting it, external borrowing for such purposes by creating SPVs may be desirable, as KIIFB reportedly proved to be after the floods in 2019. The expert committee’s recommendation to dissolve KIIFB is the easier part. In the present political milieu, efforts to boost public investments to catch up with the neighbouring States are a harder job – with the Centre strictly monitoring Keralam. The State will have to devise newer and administratively innovative means to tap OBBs, as most States do. The task is primarily a political one.

articles.title: What the new E100 vehicle rules mean | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The amendments modify Rule 115, which deals with emission standards and related requirements for motor vehicles, and Rule 115E, which contains additional provisions relating to emission testing

The story so far: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has amended the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 , to permit the use of ethanol-based fuels containing up to 100% ethanol (E100) in vehicles. The move paves the way for flex-fuel vehicles, which can run on petrol, ethanol blends of varying proportions, or pure ethanol.
The amendments modify Rule 115, which deals with emission standards and related requirements for motor vehicles, and Rule 115E, which contains additional provisions relating to emission testing.

One of the key changes is the inclusion of E100, or fuel comprising 100% ethanol, alongside E85 in several tables under Rule 115. E85 is a fuel containing up to 85% ethanol, while E100 consists entirely of ethanol, subject to applicable fuel specifications.
The amendments include an explanatory note stating that E85 or E100 may be used only in flex-fuel vehicles designed by original equipment manufacturers.

No. In a press statement, the Ministry sought to allay concerns among motorists, clarifying that a vehicle’s compatibility with E10 or E20 does not establish its suitability for E85. The notification does not require owners of existing vehicles to switch to E85 or modify their vehicles, either now or in the future.

Motorists should check the fuel-compatibility sticker on their vehicle and follow the manufacturer’s guidance in the owner’s manual when choosing fuel at a filling station, the Ministry statement added.

The amendments are expected to facilitate homologation, the official certification process through which authorised agencies, such as the Automotive Research Association of India, verify that vehicles and components comply with technical, safety and environmental standards before they can be approved for sale or use on public roads.
This will help secure type approvals for E100-powered vehicles, supporting their rollout and wider consumer adoption.
Corrections have also been incorporated into fuel classifications, including a reference to gasoline blended with 20% ethanol, or E20, in place of an earlier notation referring to E10.

India achieved its 20% ethanol-blending (E20) target in 2025 , five years ahead of the original 2030 deadline set under the National Policy on Biofuels, 2018. From April 2026, all Bharat Stage-VI (BS-VI) vehicles are required to fully meet E20 emission standards, and all petrol sold across India is mandated to contain 20% ethanol (E20). The policy focus is now widening beyond E20: the government has enabled the regulatory pathway for E85 and E100 vehicles, though these fuels will require compatible flex-fuel vehicles and dedicated dispensing infrastructure.

The main concern is vehicle compatibility. Owners of older or non-E20-compliant vehicles question whether E20 could damage components, raise maintenance costs, or leave them without access to lower-ethanol petrol.

Consumers also question E20’s effect on fuel economy. Ethanol has a lower energy density than petrol; while the government estimates a 5% decline in mileage, some consumers say the loss is greater. Dealers, meanwhile, warn that ethanol’s affinity for water could raise contamination risks during the monsoon, strengthening the case for separate storage and dispensing systems for higher blends. These concerns have prompted calls for a transparent assessment.

articles.title: At least 10 dead in crash between two trains in Spain’s Toledo province
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Spanish state broadcaster TVE is reporting that the accident was between two high-speed trains heading in the same direction and that one ran into the tail of the other, knocking two of its cars off the track
Spain’s state-owned news agency and other local media say at least 10 people have died in a crash between two trains in central Spain.
Spain’s rail system operator ADIF said the crash occurred Wednesday morning (October 28, 2026) in the province of Toledo. Rail service is suspended between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia.
TVE is reporting that the accident was between two high-speed trains heading in the same direction and that one ran into the tail of the other, knocking two of its cars off the track.

The Mayor of the nearby town of Urda, Manuel Galán, told Spanish state broadcaster TVE that passengers had been injured and that civil protection authorities had asked his town hall to prepare a sports pavilion to attend to passengers.
The Mayor of another nearby village, Jesús Pérez of Los Yébenes, told TVE that it appeared that the accident was “serious.”
The regional president of Castilla La Mancha, Emiliano García-Page, wrote on X that he is on his way to the crash site.

In January, 45 people died in southern Spain when a train jumped the track and hit an oncoming train. The crash was the deadliest in Spain since a 2013 crash that killed 80 people. The January incident shook the confidence the European country has in its extensive high-speed rail network.
