articles.title: When 43 LTTE militants escaped from Vellore Fort special camp in 1995
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The extremists, including four women, who were housed in a special camp, had dug a 153-foot tunnel from a bathroom in the Tippu Mahal to the moat. They slipped out in batches. The daring escape sent shock waves as the camp was guarded by five watchtowers and two companies of the Central Reserve Police Force that assisted the Tamil Nadu Police

Around 3 a.m. on August 15, 1995, policemen on night patrol on Sivagnanam Road at T. Nagar in Chennai stopped two men on a cycle-rickshaw. A constable noticed a handbag and tried to examine its contents. In a flash, one of the men bit a cyanide capsule tied around his neck and almost instantly dropped dead. In the confusion, the other man rode away on a cycle kept nearby with the bag. The police found a Vellore tailor shop’s label on the dead man’s shirt.

A few hours later, at the Egmore Railway Station, a policeman in plainclothes, who had worked in the ‘Q’ Branch, noticed a group of 11 waiting to board a Madurai-bound train. He found their Tamil accent different. Suspecting something, he quietly approached the Railway Police. As a posse of policemen walked towards the group, two of them bit cyanide capsules. One of them died and the other was later hospitalised. A few women constables of the Government Railway Police overpowered some of the fleeing men. Angry at being caught, some of them bit the women in a vain bid to escape.

It did not take long to conclude that the men involved in the two incidents shared a common link. All belonged to the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), the Sri Lankan Tamil outfit, which was banned in India in 1991, following the assassination of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi.

It emerged that 43 hardcore LTTE militants, including four women, all of whom were housed in a special camp in the Vellore Fort, had escaped after digging a 153-foot-long tunnel in the Tippu Mahal. The tunnel was dug from one of the bathrooms to the moat. “Two batches of six militants each escaped on the night of August 13, while a group of 11 slipped out after midnight on Monday. The rest fled afterwards,” reported The Hindu in its August 16, 1995 edition.

The daring escape had sent shock waves as the camp was well-guarded: it had five watchtowers and two companies of the Central Reserve Police Force to assist the Tamil Nadu Police. Chief Minister Jayalalithaa immediately convened a meeting with Chief Secretary N. Haribhaskar and Director-General of Police V. Vaikunth to work out a strategy to recapture the militants.

The Superintendent of Police of North Arcot-Ambedkar district (as Vellore was known then) was suspended, along with officers in charge of security at the camp. The government announced a reward of ₹10,000 for anyone sharing information about the escaped militants. It ordered a judicial inquiry headed by Justice T.N. Singaravelu, a retired judge of the Madras High Court.

This was not the first time that the LTTE militants had escaped in Tamil Nadu. In November 1992, 18 militants had escaped from the Tippu Mahal itself. In January 1991, the police opened fire in the Vellore camp, when 400-odd militants attempted to break open the window bars and attack the policemen. Some of them had climbed the terrace of the Tippu Mahal and threw stones and bricks at the policemen standing below. An attempt to set ablaze Sub-Inspector Kannappan after dousing him with kerosene was foiled. A militant, Indiran, 21, was killed in the police firing.

Yet, this was the first time that the militants had escaped by digging a tunnel. “The elaborate planning was proved by the fact that the escapees organised themselves into groups and fanned out to different areas. While one group was believed to have arrived in the city by train, another did so by bus. The direction the other groups took was not known,” wrote The Hindu in a report, ‘LTTE escape: Many questions unanswered’.

It said, “People in Vellore expressed surprise and disbelief when reporters told them about the militants’ escape by digging a tunnel using old and rusted pipes and other improvised tools. They were anxious to know whether the tunnel had been dug beyond the rampart wall of the fort. How could they do such a job when the fort had a very deep rocky foundation? they wondered.”

When journalists wanted to have a look at the tunnel on day one, the police refused permission, citing the judicial inquiry. However, on August 19, journalists from Madras were taken to inspect the tunnel, which had just an 1-1/2 foot x 1-1/2 foot entry point on the first floor of the Tippu Mahal. The exit point of 3 feet x 3 feet was located in between the fort and the moat walls on the western side.

“Both the entry and exit points looked so hideous that pressmen were reluctant to pass through the tunnel despite the readiness of the police to allow them. Commandos Sathya and Perumal told this correspondent that they could crawl through the tunnel within three minutes, though the route was zigzag at some points,” read a report. Many of the escaped militants were captured later.

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 27 Oct 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

When 43 LTTE militants escaped from Vellore Fort special camp in 1995

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

The extremists, including four women, who were housed in a special camp, had dug a 153-foot tunnel from a bathroom in the Tippu Mahal to the moat. They slipped out in batches. The daring escape sent shock waves as the camp was guarded by five watchtowers and two companies of the Central Reserve Police Force that assisted the Tamil Nadu Police

Around 3 a.m. on August 15, 1995, policemen on night patrol on Sivagnanam Road at T. Nagar in Chennai stopped two men on a cycle-rickshaw. A constable noticed a handbag and tried to examine its contents. In a flash, one of the men bit a cyanide capsule tied around his neck and almost instantly dropped dead. In the confusion, the other man rode away on a cycle kept nearby with the bag. The police found a Vellore tailor shop’s label on the dead man’s shirt.

A few hours later, at the Egmore Railway Station, a policeman in plainclothes, who had worked in the ‘Q’ Branch, noticed a group of 11 waiting to board a Madurai-bound train. He found their Tamil accent different. Suspecting something, he quietly approached the Railway Police. As a posse of policemen walked towards the group, two of them bit cyanide capsules. One of them died and the other was later hospitalised. A few women constables of the Government Railway Police overpowered some of the fleeing men. Angry at being caught, some of them bit the women in a vain bid to escape.

It did not take long to conclude that the men involved in the two incidents shared a common link. All belonged to the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), the Sri Lankan Tamil outfit, which was banned in India in 1991, following the assassination of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi.

It emerged that 43 hardcore LTTE militants, including four women, all of whom were housed in a special camp in the Vellore Fort, had escaped after digging a 153-foot-long tunnel in the Tippu Mahal. The tunnel was dug from one of the bathrooms to the moat. “Two batches of six militants each escaped on the night of August 13, while a group of 11 slipped out after midnight on Monday. The rest fled afterwards,” reported The Hindu in its August 16, 1995 edition.

The daring escape had sent shock waves as the camp was well-guarded: it had five watchtowers and two companies of the Central Reserve Police Force to assist the Tamil Nadu Police. Chief Minister Jayalalithaa immediately convened a meeting with Chief Secretary N. Haribhaskar and Director-General of Police V. Vaikunth to work out a strategy to recapture the militants.

The Superintendent of Police of North Arcot-Ambedkar district (as Vellore was known then) was suspended, along with officers in charge of security at the camp. The government announced a reward of ₹10,000 for anyone sharing information about the escaped militants. It ordered a judicial inquiry headed by Justice T.N. Singaravelu, a retired judge of the Madras High Court.

This was not the first time that the LTTE militants had escaped in Tamil Nadu. In November 1992, 18 militants had escaped from the Tippu Mahal itself. In January 1991, the police opened fire in the Vellore camp, when 400-odd militants attempted to break open the window bars and attack the policemen. Some of them had climbed the terrace of the Tippu Mahal and threw stones and bricks at the policemen standing below. An attempt to set ablaze Sub-Inspector Kannappan after dousing him with kerosene was foiled. A militant, Indiran, 21, was killed in the police firing.

Yet, this was the first time that the militants had escaped by digging a tunnel. “The elaborate planning was proved by the fact that the escapees organised themselves into groups and fanned out to different areas. While one group was believed to have arrived in the city by train, another did so by bus. The direction the other groups took was not known,” wrote The Hindu in a report, ‘LTTE escape: Many questions unanswered’.

It said, “People in Vellore expressed surprise and disbelief when reporters told them about the militants’ escape by digging a tunnel using old and rusted pipes and other improvised tools. They were anxious to know whether the tunnel had been dug beyond the rampart wall of the fort. How could they do such a job when the fort had a very deep rocky foundation? they wondered.”

When journalists wanted to have a look at the tunnel on day one, the police refused permission, citing the judicial inquiry. However, on August 19, journalists from Madras were taken to inspect the tunnel, which had just an 1-1/2 foot x 1-1/2 foot entry point on the first floor of the Tippu Mahal. The exit point of 3 feet x 3 feet was located in between the fort and the moat walls on the western side.

“Both the entry and exit points looked so hideous that pressmen were reluctant to pass through the tunnel despite the readiness of the police to allow them. Commandos Sathya and Perumal told this correspondent that they could crawl through the tunnel within three minutes, though the route was zigzag at some points,” read a report. Many of the escaped militants were captured later.

articles.title: Theni jailbreak: Efforts are on to nab escaped prisoners who are still absconding, says T.N. Law Minister Nirmal Kumar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar rejects political vendetta charge over former DMK Minister Anbil Mahesh’s arrest

Tamil Nadu Minister for Energy Resources and Law C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar, speaking to reporters in Coimbatore on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), said efforts are under way to nab 13 of the 17 prisoners who escaped from District Jail at Thekkampatti in Theni district the previous night.

Commenting on the jailbreak in which 17 remand prisoners escaped from the prison after they allegedly assaulted three prison guards, the Minister said four of them had been arrested and efforts were under way to trace and apprehend the remaining 13 prisoners.
Theni jailbreak: Human error led to escape of prisoners, says DGP-Prisons Sandeep Rai Rathore; nine guards suspended
When 43 LTTE militants escaped from Vellore Fort special camp in 1995

Checks have been intensified at checkpoints including those along the Kerala border and in forest areas. Director-General of Prisons and Correctional Services Sandeep Rai Rathore and the Inspector-General of Police are inspecting in person to ascertain whether there had been any security lapses, the Minister added.

Further, responding to former Chief Minister and DMK president M.K. Stalin’s allegation that the arrest of former School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi was an act of political vendetta, the Minister rejected the claims. He said the investigation into the allegations against Mr. Poyyamozhi would proceed according to law.
Mr. Nirmal Kumar alleged that more than ₹400 crores had been collected from schools in the name of ‘party funds’ through a certificate related to school safety during Mr. Poyyamozhi’s tenure

He also accused the DMK of threatening educational institutions into making payments. He claimed that schools run by non-governmental organisations, Christian missionary groups and trusts had also faced pressure and said more institutions were now coming forward to lodge complaints.

Referring to remark — “they should have finished him off in Karur that very day” — allegedly made by Mr. Poyyamozhi’s supporters outside the court in Chennai, the Minister alleged that the statement raised questions about possible prior planning in connection with the 2025 Karur stampede.

On the death of Coimbatore school student A. Akilan by suicide , he said the police had been given a free hand to investigate the case and that there would be no political pressure. He said anyone found to have committed a crime would be dealt with in accordance with the law.

On rooftop solar installations, Mr. Nirmal Kumar said Tamil Nadu had installed 87,000 systems by April and had received more than 27,000 applications in the subsequent five months. The government aimed to install rooftop solar systems in one lakh houses by March (2027), with around 10,000 applications already processed.

He also said the government was reviewing fixed electricity charges and would announce the outcome of its assessment within a week. Long-term power purchase agreements for more than 4,000 MW were planned, subject to approval from the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission.

articles.title: Sudan drone strikes kill 21, cause mass outages in east amid ongoing violence
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A drone strike on a market in Nyala, the de facto capital of Sudan’s paramilitary RSF, in Darfur, killed 21 people and wounded at least 40 others, a medical source and witnesses told AFP

Sudan's warring sides have traded drone strikes that killed 21 people in the western Darfur region and left vast swathes of the country's east without electricity, medics and witnesses said on Tuesday (October 27, 2026).

A drone strike on a market in Nyala, the de facto capital of Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Darfur, killed 21 people and wounded at least 40 others, a medical source and witnesses told AFP .
One Nyala resident said a market in the city's north was struck by a drone on Monday (October 26, 2026) around 8:00 p.m. (1800 GMT).
Another said the market was frequented by young men, particularly RSF fighters.
"Twenty-one people were killed in last night's bombing, and more than 40 others injured," a medic at Nyala hospital said, though he was unable to identify how many were RSF fighters.

Sudan's military, at war with the RSF since April 2023, regularly strikes Nyala, where the RSF has declared an administration rivalling the Army-backed internationally recognised government in Khartoum.
The RSF has in turn launched repeated strikes targeting Khartoum's airport, as well as dams and power stations across the country's east.

On Tuesday (October 27, 2026), "RSF militia drones targeted the Al-Markhiyat transformer station, disrupting the power supply across large parts of Khartoum and Al-Jazira states," a source in the national electricity company told AFP on condition of anonymity.
The strike comes a day after a coordinated RSF drone attack on six power stations left millions without power in Al-Jazira, White Nile, Sennar and Gedaref states.
The war is currently being fought primarily via drones, with both sides launching sophisticated attacks from across the country, killing dozens of civilians at a time.
In the first three weeks of October alone, drone strikes killed over 300 people and injured hundreds more, according to a UN tally.
Sudan army shoots down RSF drones near Khartoum: military source

articles.title: New UNSC permanent members without veto would be 'second-class': India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: India said the veto must be held by all permanent members of a reformed Council as long as the provision exists, stressing that fairness and justice demand equal rights and responsibilities for all permanent members

India has asserted that any reform of the UN Security Council that creates a new category of permanent members without veto powers would effectively relegate them to “second-class” status, leaving the existing five permanent powers in control of the decision-making process.

China, France, Russia, the U.K. and the U.S. are the five permanent members of the 15-member Security Council and enjoy veto powers. The Council also has 10 non-permanent members elected for two-year terms.

India's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, on Monday (October 26, 2026) said the veto must be held by all permanent members of a reformed Council as long as the provision exists, stressing that fairness and justice demand equal rights and responsibilities for all permanent members.
"India's position on the veto is principled and well known... We reiterate that as long as the veto exists, it must be held by all permanent members of a reformed Council," he said.

Addressing the Inter-Governmental (IGN) plenary on 'Cluster Debate on the Question of the Veto' in the UN General Assembly, Parvathaneni said a reform that expands the Security Council by "creating another category of long-term members without the veto effectively makes them 'second-class' members and would not change the decision-making dynamic of the P5".

Creating a new category of permanent members, with or without veto powers, would further complicate an already difficult discussion and "entrench the very inequity we are seeking to correct", he said.
"Periodic elections and the concept of permanency are fundamentally contradictory,” the diplomat said.

“History has a lesson for us,” he said, recalling that the only expansion of the Security Council, in 1965, increased the number of non-permanent members from six to 10 while retaining five permanent members.
The ratio of permanent to elected members shifted from 5:6 to 5:10, further strengthening the relative power of the P5, Mr. Parvathaneni said.

India has consistently called for expanding both the permanent and non-permanent categories of membership, warning that reform efforts would border on "failure" if they focused solely on increasing the number of non-permanent members.

New Delhi has been at the forefront of years-long efforts to achieve reform of the Security Council, saying the body, founded in 1945, is not fit for purpose in the 21st century and does not reflect contemporary geopolitical realities.
India has consistently underscored that it rightly deserves a permanent seat at the horse-shoe table.

• India said the veto must be held by all permanent members of a reformed Council as long as the provision exists, stressing that fairness and justice demand equal rights and responsibilities for all permanent members
• India has asserted that any reform of the UN Security Council that creates a new category of permanent members without veto powers would effectively relegate them to “second-class” status, leaving the existing five permanent powers in control of the decision-making process.
• China, France, Russia, the U.K. and the U.S. are the five permanent members of the 15-member Security Council and enjoy veto powers. The Council also has 10 non-permanent members elected for two-year terms.

articles.title: U.S. judge halts tree-cutting at Trump’s golf course project
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: District Judge Ana Reyes ordered a halt after more than 500 trees were felled at East Potomac Golf Links, as Trump pledged to appeal and vowed to proceed with the November 15 renovation
A U.S. federal judge ruled on Monday (October 26, 2026) to halt tree-cutting at a public golf course in the heart of the capital, after hundreds of trees were felled in Donald Trump's pet project.

An avid golfer who owns courses around the world, the U.S. President has called for Washington's East Potomac Golf Links, a public course with affordable rates, to be remodelled into a facility capable of hosting major championship-calibre events.

The early demolition for the overhaul had charged ahead despite an environmental group's lawsuit, and opposition from local golfers who argue the 100-year-old course is a rare spot where they can affordably play the sport.

"The Court ENJOINS defendants from removing or damaging additional trees on East Potomac Golf Course and ORDERS them to provide ten business days' written advance notice before making any irreparable modification to any forms or features of East Potomac Park, pending the outcome of this litigation," District Judge Ana Reyes wrote in Monday's 70-page order.

"The Government felled hundreds of trees from the East Potomac Golf Course without real notice, even though it knew of the scheduled removal at least a week prior," Ms. Reyes said, adding that they were "healthy, nonhazardous trees."

Mr. Trump said this month that construction was set to start in November on the 18-hole course. He insisted on Monday that the site would close for renovation as scheduled, on November 15, and pledged to appeal Ms. Reyes' decision.
"The judge has absolutely no right to hold up this very important and beautiful Project," Mr. Trump wrote on Truth Social.
More than 500 trees have already been cut down, the judge wrote.
The court "does not speak for the trees," Ms. Reyes wrote in her order, in reference to the Dr. Seuss book The Lorax.

articles.title: Why scratching an itch feel so good
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Scratch, scratch… and then you hit the exact spot. Aah, yes! We have all had that satisfying moment when a stubborn itch finally disappears under our fingernails. But why does scratching an itch feel so good, and sometimes even feel pleasurable?

As it turns out, scientists have wondered about this too. There is even a research paper titled “The Pleasurability of Scratching an Itch”. Yes, you read that right. So, what exactly is going on between your skin, nerves and brain when you scratch? Let’s find out.

Seems like a weird question? Well, science turns every weird question into a curious one. That is why, an itch is more than just an annoying feeling on your skin. It is a signal from your body telling you that something may be irritating it. Specialised nerve cells in your skin detect the irritation and send signals through your nerves to your spinal cord and brain. Your brain then registers the sensation as an itch — and that is when you get the urge to scratch.
When you scratch an itchy spot, the action activates pain-sensing nerves in your skin. These signals travel to the spinal cord and brain and can temporarily suppress the itch signals.

But there is another player: serotonin. Scratching can cause the release of serotonin in the spinal cord. While serotonin is often associated with feelings such as happiness and well-being, in this case it can also affect how the brain processes itch and pain. It helps dampen the itch for a while, giving you that satisfying feeling of relief.
The catch? Serotonin can also activate certain itch-related nerve cells, which may explain why the relief from scratching is temporary — and why you may soon want to scratch again.

So, why does scratching feel not just relieving, but actually good? Part of the answer lies in the brain’s response to the sensation. Scratching provides a strong physical sensation that competes with the itch, while the sudden drop in discomfort brings a feeling of relief.

That contrast, going from “ugh, this is itchy” to “ahh, finally!” can make scratching feel surprisingly satisfying. In other words, your brain is not only noticing the scratch; it is also enjoying the relief that follows.

That satisfying scratch can come with a downside. Scratching too much can damage the skin, cause inflammation and even lead to small cuts that allow bacteria to enter. In some cases, the irritation can make the itching worse — giving you another reason to scratch.
Apparently, yes. In the study, researchers induced an itch at three different spots — the forearm, ankle and back — and then measured how intense the itch felt and how pleasurable scratching was.

The ankle and back produced stronger itch sensations than the forearm. Interestingly, scratching was also rated as more pleasurable at these two sites. On the back, scratching was particularly effective at reducing the itch.

The researchers also found that the stronger the itch, the greater the pleasure from scratching at the forearm and ankle. So, when an itch is really bothering you, finally hitting the right spot may feel even more satisfying.

articles.title: Apple launches new iPad Mini, powered by A20 Pro chip and thinner design
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Apple’s new iPad mini comes with a larger 8.5-inch OLED display, and is 5.4mm thin
Apple unveiled the new iPad mini, with the company touting its “biggest update ever,” as the tablet clocks in with a width of 5.4 mm.

The iPad mini features an 8.5-inch OLED display, with peak brightness of up to 1,200 nits and support for 600 nits of full-screen brightness for SDR and HDR content. It has a 1-nit minimum brightness level, along with a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
Powered by a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each GPU core, the new iPad mini runs on A20 Pro, with the iPhone-maker promising enhanced graphics and AI-intensive tasks.

The 12MP Center Stage front camera is located on the landscape edge, while the 12MP Wide back camera supports Smart HDR 4 and 4K video at up to 60 fps. There is an Adaptive True Tone flash for photos and document scanning.
iPad mini users will be able to access Siri AI, which is rolling out in beta with iPadOS 27.
The device comes with a water and dust-resistance rating of IP67.
Customers can pre-order the new iPad mini and the new Smart Folio from October 28, with availability beginning November 6.
The iPad mini will be available in the Midnight and Starlight variants, with 128GB, 256GB, and 512GB configurations.
The iPad mini starts at ₹82,900 for the Wi-Fi model, and ₹1,00,900 for the Wi-Fi + Cellular model. This represents a major jump in price for the device.
The iPad mini starts at ₹76,900 with education savings.

“iPad mini is beloved for its fantastic portability, performance, and display by a wide range of users, from creators and small business owners to doctors, field service workers, and gamers. With a remarkably thinner and lighter design, a stunning new OLED display, the incredibly powerful A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance, the new iPad mini is a huge leap forward for users who love having the full iPad experience in the palm of their hand,” said Dave Pakula, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering.

articles.title: Into the “brain rot” psyche
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Bringing pop culture, internet, nonsense, and scientists together, the teenage slang word ‘brain rot’ is a phenomenon overall. Here’s an insightful look into what exactly it is and its implications in the ways of our life.
Here, feed it this reel. And another one. This one’s just a cat doing a dance challenge. Simply harmless. Yes, harmless. Like it to get more.
Time pass? Boredom? The all-knowing algorithm will take care of it. Keep liking. Don’t stop.
Reality is too complex. No words to describe it? Watch this reel. More and some more. The brain is quiet.

Researchers, scientists and doctors alike have always fussed over the brain, psychologically and medically. Contemporary internet culture gives them another reason to do it — brain rot. It was named the Oxford Word of the Year in 2024 . Surely, we have heard all about it.

Brain rot’s public fame from the confines of social media brought to light several serious concerns regarding the effects of present-day social media use patterns on the brain, typically among the younger generation who relatively have an upperhand when it comes to grasping and using digital tech.
Illustration by Esra Eslen. | Photo Credit: Wikimedia Commons

Doomscrolling, low attention span, feedback loop, instant gratification, too much screen time, overstimulation, memory disruption, etc. stand out as aspects fuelling a collective brain rot. As the word suggests, the idea is one of rotting — rotting of the high intelligence and cognition that puts humans on the top among the creatures of Earth. How interestingly ironic it is, this concept, culturally perceiving that the same intelligence that created all this brilliant tech is mediating the ‘rotting’.

Let’s put aside the negative connotations and start with a clean plate. Initially, brain rot’s popularity had brought immense panic among the adults. It was a threat and some even viewed it as a sort of “Gen-Z disease”. The thing is, brain rot is somewhere between a pop label and mental malady which means arguments on and around the concept are continuously being shaped and reshaped. The behaviours and effects are still being monitored.

Interestingly, some brain science and psychology studies this year have described brainrot as participatory, allaying the particularly gloomy theme that it is a downgrading cognitive characteristic of an entire generation of teenagers. These studies highlight two important things about the psyche of brainrot — how we use our free time and participation. It challenges the notion of brain rot as a helpless passive setup that affects all youth. The baton is in our hands. Let’s analyse this again.

When do we use social media mostly? During free time. Now, in my free time, if I like a short reel video and more videos like that pop up on my feed, I’m the participant participating in the algorithm, aren’t I? A 2026 study by Emilie Owens published in the journal New Media & Society revealed that brain rot can be understood as “decompression-driven” and that teenagers are “actively resisting” productivity similar to how people binge-watch or even play games. Huh, very interesting. Imagine I’m home after work and my brain is filled with thoughts related to work. I need my brain to shut up, so I open social media for quick distraction and relaxation. If it were years back, after coming from school, I would likely go out to play instead. If a 40-something guy started using social media right now and drove the algorithm to keep giving him all these new varieties of low-quality and unchallenging reels, isn’t he also a citizen of the brainrot kingdom?

Chaithanya N C, a neuropsychologist at the Ananthapuri Hospital and Research Institute, pointed out the larger case — “it is not that teenagers are at fault, rather, the digital environment is set up that way and in this case, demanding such ultra-short, nonsensical videos to grab their attention.” Owens notes that binge-watching has an end point, i.e. when the show ends, whereas scrolling is infinite. The social media algorithmic bias driven by feedback loops (user interactions are taken as triggers which shape the future content) point to a need that the person using the social media has to have a greater awareness and control of the information they get.

Chaithanya says, “AI in itself is not strictly causative of brain rot, but the type of content consumed and the need for engagement may be associated with brain rot. AI tools make it easier to generate large amounts of repetitive, absurd, or low-quality content that can induce mental states of brain rot, which include fragmented attention, a need for constant stimulation to escape boredom and doomscrolling.”

The social media algorithmic bias driven by feedback loops (user interactions are taken as triggers which shape the future content) point to a need that the person using the social media has to have a greater awareness and control of the information they get.

Chaithanya says, “AI in itself is not strictly causative of brain rot, but the type of content consumed and the need for engagement may be associated with brain rot. AI tools make it easier to generate large amounts of repetitive, absurd, or low-quality content that can induce mental states of brain rot, which include fragmented attention, a need for constant stimulation to escape boredom and doomscrolling.”

articles.title: Action sought against Periyar University professor for participating in DMK function
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Former president of Periyar University Teachers Association (PUTA) V. Vaithianathan on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) submitted a petition seeking action against a professor for allegedly participating in a function organised by a political party earlier this month.

In a petition, accompanied by photographs and submitted to Periyar University Registrar (in-charge) V. Raj on Tuesday, Mr. Vaithianathan said that R. Subramani, Head of the Department of Journalism and Mass Communication, had allegedly participated in a DMK function (the unveiling of a portrait of a DMK functionary) organised in Perambalur district on October 15. Mr. Subramani participated in the function alongside former Union Minister A. Raja.

Mr. Vaithianathan said they chatted on the dais and later in a separate room. On October 15, Mr. Subramani took casual leave and participated in the function. As per Periyar University rules, “No employee shall be a member of any political organisation or take active part in any political activity. No university employee shall associate himself with or take an active part in politics,” Mr. Vaithianathan said.

Stating that Mr. Subramani had clearly violated the rules, the former PUTA president said that Mr. Subramani had served as a member of the Periyar University Vice-Chancellor Committee and the Syndicate. He had also applied for the post of Registrar of Periyar University. Mr. Vaithianathan said Mr. Subramani knew the university’s rules but had allegedly violated them intentionally.

An essay by Mr. Subramani had also been published in a book released by the DMK. According to Mr. Vaithianathan, Mr. Subramani’s participation in the function clearly indicated that he was an active member of a political party. “So, the university should place him under suspension immediately, and a committee should be formed to inquire into the allegations. Likewise, decisions made during his term as a member of the Vice-Chancellor Committee should be reviewed, and action should be taken if any decisions were found to have been made with a political agenda,” Mr. Vaithianathan added.
When contacted, Mr. Subramani was not available for comment. He also did not respond to the messages sent by The Hindu .

When contacted, Mr. Raj said that he had received the complaint on Tuesday. “We will take up the issue with the convenor of the Periyar University Vice-Chancellor Committee and take further action based on the convenor’s instructions,” the Periyar University Registrar (in-charge) added.

articles.title: At SCO meet, Rajnath calls for dismantling the entire ecosystem of terrorism
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: There is no place for those who finance, support, or provide safe havens to terrorists, says Defence Minister; India supports adoption of action plan for trade and economic cooperation among SCO members

There can be no justification for terrorism and no double standards in tackling the menace, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said on Tuesday, called on the member states of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) to dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism.
He was speaking at the 25th meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of Government in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, in the presence of Pakistan’s Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar.

“Terrorism results in the loss of innocent lives and disrupts investment and commerce. It radicalises societies and deprives youth of the opportunities they rightfully deserve. There can be no justification for terrorism, no double standards in addressing it, and no place for those who finance, support, or provide safe havens to terrorists,” Mr. Singh said.

He recalled Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s remarks at the SCO Summit in Bishkek in August and September, calling for concrete steps on security, connectivity, and opportunity. Mr. Singh said the organisation must adhere to the principles of sovereign equality, consensus, and mutual respect.

On economic cooperation, the Defence Minister called for strengthening resilient supply chains, facilitating trade and investment, and leveraging technology to address global uncertainties arising from geopolitical tensions, trade disruptions, and concerns over energy and food security. India supported the adoption of an action plan for the multilateral trade and economic cooperation programme for the period 2026-2030, he said.

New SCO mechanisms should address clearly identified needs and avoid duplication, Mr. Singh said. He welcomed the decisions to establish the Universal Centre in Tashkent and the Anti-Drug Centre in Dushanbe as permanent SCO bodies, while stressing the need for effective coordination and timely implementation.

Highlighting regional connectivity, he noted initiatives such as the International North-South Transport Corridor and Chabahar Port could connect Central Asia with wider markets. However, connectivity projects must respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries, he said.

The Defence Minister also highlighted India’s digital public infrastructure, start-up ecosystem, and women-led development initiatives, alongside its international efforts on clean energy and climate resilience.
The meeting reviewed economic and trade cooperation among member States and discussed transport, finance, the digital economy, and social development.

The Heads of Delegation adopted a joint communiqué, the SCO budget for 2027, and the action plan for multilateral trade and economic cooperation for 2026-2030. Mr. Singh also invited member States to participate in the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, to be hosted by India later this year.

articles.title: Days after India-Pakistan sparring at UN, senior Indian official visits Islamabad for SCO planning meet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: First such official visit by Indian delegation since Operation Indoor; Senior External Affair Ministry official leads team at three-day SCO preparatory meeting

Pakistan announced that it would host the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in August 2027, as an Indian delegation led by a senior MEA official attended a preparatory meeting in Islamabad—the first such official Indian visit to Pakistan since Operation Sindoor last year.

The three-day meeting of SCO National Coordinators that began on Monday (September 29, 2026) comes days after India and Pakistan sparred with each other over the issue of terrorism and the Kashmir dispute at the UN General Assembly (UNGA). External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif traded allegations in their national addresses, while Indian and Pakistani diplomats exercised their rights of reply to the speeches on the global stage last week.
On Tuesday (September 29, 2026), India also rejected Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s reference to Kashmir in his UNGA speech.

The participation of Joint Secretary (Multilaterals and Economic Relations) Alok Dimri marked a higher level of Indian representation than at the past few meetings held under Pakistan’s Chairpersonship of the SCO this year. In mid-September, a meeting of SCO-Regional Anti-Terror Structure in Islamabad was attended by the Indian Charge d’affaires in Pakistan Satyapal Pandey, without a delegation from India.

In a statement, the Pakistan Ministry of Foreign Affairs said that Pakistan’s SCO Chairship would promote the theme of “Turning Vision into Action: Connectivity, Innovation and Shared Prosperity,” for 2026-207.

“The [National Coordinator] meeting marks an important initial engagement under Pakistan’s Chairmanship and would contribute to preparations for various high-level engagements and activities to be undertaken during the Chairmanship, including the meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of State to be hosted by Pakistan in August 2027,” the MoFA statement issued in Islamabad said.

Indian officials made it clear that the SCO coordinators’ meet was being held in a multilateral format and hence had no particular significance for India-Pakistan bilateral ties. However, the participation does leave the path open to higher-level attendance at the Ministerial-level events and the Heads of Council meet, to which Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been invited. Thus far, New Delhi has avoided the leaders’ meetings in both Delhi and Islamabad.

In 2023, PM Modi hosted the SCO Heads of Council Summit virtually, while Mr. Jaishankar hosted Pakistani Foreign Minister Bilawal Bhutto in person for the SCO Foreign Ministers’ meeting in Goa. In 2024, Mr. Jaishankar travelled to Islamabad to attend the SCO Heads of Government meeting as well. The MEA has thus far declined to comment on whether Mr. Modi would travel to Pakistan next year, but has not ruled it out either.

At a briefing on Tuesday (September 29, 2026), MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal brushed aside a question about whether India would oppose the induction of Turkiye to the 10-nation SCO, which currently comprises China, Russia, India, Pakistan, Iran, Belarus and four Central Asian States- Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan.

Turkish President Erdogan had told journalists earlier this month that Türkiye would pursue a “higher level” of engagement with the SCO than its observer status, indicating he could ask for full membership next year, particularly given close ties and the military pact with SCO host Pakistan.

“As and when any issue of membership comes it is for [SCO] members to collectively decide as to how to go forward on that,” Mr. Jaiswal said. He also criticised Mr. Erdogan for referring to Kashmir in his UNGA speech last week, when he called for a resolution of all South Asian disputes “including Kashmir”.

“India rejects the unwarranted references to India and the Indian Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir made by the President of Türkiye during his address to the UN General Assembly. This is a matter, as you would understand, pertaining to India’s territorial integrity and sovereignty, and no external party has any locus standi on this issue,” Mr. Jaiswal said on Tuesday.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu government extends ban on inter-State transport of rough stones by three months
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State government had issued a temporary ban on transportation of rough stones and their aggregates to other States (except Puducherry and the Karaikal region) on July 27 for a period of three months

The Tamil Nadu government has extended the temporary ban imposed on transportation of rough stones and their aggregates to other States, except to Puducherry and the Karaikal region, for another three months from October 27.

The State government had issued a temporary ban on transportation of rough stones and their aggregates to other States, except to Puducherry and the Karaikal region, on July 27 for a period of three months. As the ban expired on October 26, the State government extended it by another three months under Rule 3(A) of the Tamil Nadu Prevention of Illegal Mining, Transportation and Storage of Minerals and Minerals Dealers Rules, 2011.
Kerala CM urges Tamil Nadu counterpart Vijay to ease restrictions on stone aggregate transport
Watch: Tamil Nadu’s stone transport ban: What’s happening? | Focus Tamil Nadu
Plea in Madras HC challenges Tamil Nadu government’s three-month ban on inter-State transport of minor minerals

When the ban was imposed three months ago, the State government said the objective was to ensure uninterrupted supply of minerals within the State, ensure the protection of the environment and ecology, and prevent illegal mining and transportation.

“The objectives of the ban have not been fully achieved during the said period. articles.title: India poised to refine for world as global capacity declines: Union Minister Hardeep Puri
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: India's refining capacity is currently around 290 million tonnes per annum and is expected to expand further, he said

India is poised to strengthen its position as a global refining hub, with its oil processing capacity set to rise to 300 million tonnes annually by 2030 even as Europe and other parts of the Western world see refinery capacity decline, Union Minister Hardeep Singh Puri said on Tuesday (October 27, 2026).

India's refining capacity is currently around 290 million tonnes per annum and is expected to expand further by scaling up existing facilities and adding new projects, the Union Petroleum Minister said at a news conference on the sidelines of the 29th Energy Technology and Innovation Meet in south Goa.

He said the expansion will allow India not only to meet its domestic energy requirements but also to supply more petroleum products to international markets. "With refining capacity increasing in a big way, we will be in the happy situation of not only refining for ourselves, but for the world," Mr. Puri added.

He contrasted India's expanding refining infrastructure with the decline in global capacity, particularly in Europe, where he estimated that at least 2,50,000 barrels per day of refining capacity was being lost annually.

"Others are going down. Ours is going up," the minister said, pointing to the expansion of Indian refineries at a time when smaller and less efficient facilities in other markets are struggling with logistical costs and operational inefficiencies.
Mr. Puri said India's refining capacity would reach 300 million tonnes per annum by 2030, though the projection may not include all new greenfield refineries in the pipeline.

He said several existing refineries are expanding capacity, with facilities of three million tonnes per annum scaling up to six million tonnes and those with six million tonnes expanding to nine million tonnes.
The Minister also cited the expansion plans of individual refiners to underline India's ability to increase supplies of petroleum products, including diesel, to both domestic and overseas markets.

Responding to questions on whether India would need to restrict exports to ensure domestic availability, Mr. Puri said the country's expanding production capacity would enable it to cater to both markets. "We are in a position to supply more to domestic and more to outside," he said.

Mr. Puri said Indian refiners had been planning capacity and production increases even when domestic diesel consumption growth was subdued, allowing the industry to prepare for higher output as demand patterns evolve.
He also pointed to the absence of new greenfield refineries in the Western world in recent decades, contrasting it with India's continued investments in refining infrastructure.

The Minister said the government's policy direction and the expansion of India's energy sector would further strengthen the country's position in global markets. "Beyond conventional petroleum products, initiatives such as Samudra Manthan and GOBARdhan (Galvanising Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan) are also expected to gain momentum, he said, adding that these developments would complement the country's expanding energy infrastructure.

articles.title: IndusInd Bank posts profit of ₹1,242 crores in Q2; asset quality improvement and interest income drives growth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The bank’s bottom line for Q2FY27 was supported by a rise in net interest income, which stood at ₹4,569 crore as against ₹4,409 crores a year ago

IndusInd Bank Limited posted a net profit of ₹1,242 crore for the quarter ended September, up 20% sequentially and trimming net loss of ₹437 for the same quarter in the preceding year. The bank had incurred net loss for the same period in previous year due to an increase in microfinance provisioning and write-offs.

The bank’s bottom line for Q2FY27 was supported by a rise in net interest income, which stood at ₹4,569 crore as against ₹4,409 crores a year ago. Sequentially, interest income declined by 2%. NII for half year (H1FY27) rose to ₹9,254, up 2.3% on year.

Asset quality of the bank improved substantially, with gross non-performing assets (NPA) ratio at 2.73% compared to 3.60% on year and net NPA declining to 0.83% from 1.04% in Q2FY26. However, the net interest margin of the bank slipped to 3.23% from 3.32% a year ago.

Net revenue of the bank for the period rose to ₹6,817 crores compared to ₹6,00 crores a year. A decline in operating expenses also helped push the bottom-line numbers, with expenses slipping to ₹3,943 crores in July-Septemeber from ₹4,013 crore for the same period last year.
Deposits of the bank rose 10% year-on-year to ₹4.28 crores. Advances of the bank for the period stood at 3.63 crores.
IndusInd held provisions of $9,012 crore as of September 30, with the provision coverage ratio at 70%.

IndusInd Bank raised nearly $3.5 billion via the Reserve Bank of India’s special window for foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) account, which was impacted the contraction in NIM. The bank said recovery in margin related to FCNR-B is expected over the next two quarters.

“Q2 reflects the growing strength of the IndusInd Bank franchise and the progress we have made in rebuilding momentum across the business. Our Q2 results demonstrate that the growth has strengthened, profitability has improved, asset quality trends remain encouraging, and our funding profile is becoming more granular and resilient,” Rajiv Anand, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of IndusInd Bank said.

The bank also informed the exchanges on Friday (October 23, 2026) that the Board of Directors of the lender has appointed Priyanka Sinha as an Additional Director in the category of Non-Executive Independent Director for a period of four consecutive years, till October 22, 2030.

Speaking to the media at post-earnings conference call, the bank said it remains confident of reaching a 1% exit return on assets for FY27. Bank also expects loans growth momentum to continue driven by retail and wholesale lending. Shares of IndusInd Bank Ltd closed at ₹835.00 on Friday, down 1.76%, on the BSE.

articles.title: Two men charged with U.K. national security offences over incident at U.S.-run military base in England
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: British-Iranian dual national Mohmed Abdulkarim and British citizen Nouman Essghir, both aged 24 and from London, were charged under the National Security Act, U.K. prosecutors say
Two men were charged on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) with national security offences over a suspected plot against RAF Fairford, a U.S.-run military air base in England, police and prosecutors said.

British-Iranian dual national Mohmed Abdulkarim and British citizen Nouman Essghir, both aged 24 and from London, were charged under the National Security Act, the Crown Prosecution Service said. They are due to appear in court later on Tuesday (October 27, 2026).
Abdulkarim is charged with assisting Iran’s intelligence service and Essghir with entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the U.K.
RAF Fairford, in western England, has been used by American bombers to strike Iran during this year’s war.

Essghir was arrested outside the base on September 27, when armed police officers and Army bomb-disposal experts swarmed the rural area. Scores of residents were evacuated from their homes as police and army bomb-disposal experts searched for explosives.
Police later said they had found a quantity of an accelerant — gasoline — in vans at the scene, but no explosives.
Essghir was initially released on bail before being re-arrested last week. Abdulkarim was arrested in the past week. Six other men have been arrested and released on bail as investigations continue.

British authorities have linked Tehran to the incident, which led the U.S. to pull its bombers from RAF Fairford. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that the apparent plot was “almost certainly” directed by Iran’s Revolutionary Guard.
Iran has denied involvement, although it has previously said that it considers any base used to attack its territory a legitimate target.
Earlier this month, the head of Britain’s MI5 spy agency warned that both Iran and Russia were expanding their attacks against the U.K., and that the RAF Fairford incident was not unique.

Ken McCallum, who leads the U.K.’s domestic security service, said Tehran is seeking to intensify its attacks in Britain beyond the traditional targets of Iranians opposed to the country’s Islamic authorities. He said more than 50 people have been arrested over Iran-linked plots in the past year.

“We have seen a range of incidents in recent months that we believe have been directed by the Iranian state, and as the director general of MI5 said just the other week, we are working together to intervene, identify and respond to that threat,” said Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, the head of National Counter Terrorism Policing in the U.K.

British authorities have linked Tehran to the incident, which led the U.S. to pull its bombers from RAF Fairford. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that the apparent plot was “almost certainly” directed by Iran’s Revolutionary Guard.

Iran has denied involvement, although it has previously said that it considers any base used to attack its territory a legitimate target.

Earlier this month, the head of Britain’s MI5 spy agency warned that both Iran and Russia were expanding their attacks against the U.K., and that the RAF Fairford incident was not unique.

Ken McCallum, who leads the U.K.’s domestic security service, said Tehran is seeking to intensify its attacks in Britain beyond the traditional targets of Iranians opposed to the country’s Islamic authorities. He said more than 50 people have been arrested over Iran-linked plots in the past year.

“We have seen a range of incidents in recent months that we believe have been directed by the Iranian state, and as the director general of MI5 said just the other week, we are working together to intervene, identify and respond to that threat,” said Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, the head of National Counter Terrorism Policing in the U.K.

articles.title: Mass outages in Sudan after RSF drones hit five power stations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The drones hit two power stations each in the states of Al-Jazira and Gedaref, and one in White Nile state, "resulting in power outages across large parts of these three states", the official said on condition of anonymity

Sudan's Paramilitary Rapid Support Forces launched a coordinated drone attack Monday (October 26, 2026) against five power stations, causing mass power outages across the country's east, a government official told AFP .

The drones hit two power stations each in the states of Al-Jazira and Gedaref, and one in White Nile state, "resulting in power outages across large parts of these three states", the official said on condition of anonymity.
All three states are controlled by the Sudanese army, which has since April 2023 been at war with its former ally, the RSF.
The United Nations has repeatedly warned that regular attacks on power stations threaten health and services for millions of people, already facing the world's largest hunger crisis.
An AFP correspondent in Al-Jazira state reported the electricity had been out since 2 a.m. (0000 GMT).
Babiker Youssef, a resident of Al-Fao in Gedaref, said the power there had also been out since the same time.
"My son is diabetic; his insulin has to be stored in the fridge," he told AFP over the phone, scared he would not be able to replace the medication if it spoils.
"We have no idea when the power will come back," he added.

Electricity has been cut for days at a time after past Paramilitary drone strikes on power stations and hydroelectric dams, compounding the suffering of nearly 20 million people facing extreme hunger.
Sudan's war is currently being fought primarily via drones, with both sides launching sophisticated attacks from across the country, killing dozens of civilians at a time.
In the first three weeks of October alone, drone strikes killed over 300 people and injured hundreds more, according to a UN tally.
Africa's third-largest country, home to an estimated 50 million people, has been ravaged by the war, which aid workers estimate has killed more than 200,000 people.

articles.title: The Hindu, Kauvery Hospital to host stroke care webinar on October 28
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The webinar will discuss early diagnosis, symptom recognition, and the importance of timely access to specialised care
The Hindu , in association with Kauvery Hospital, will organise a webinar on stroke care on October 28, 2026, ahead of World Stroke Day, observed on October 29.

Titled ‘The Golden Hour: Every Minute Matters, Every Life Counts’, the webinar will be held at 11.30 a.m. as part of Kauvery Hospital’s Wellness Series. It will discuss the importance of early diagnosis, advances in stroke treatment, and the need for timely access to appropriate care.

A stroke occurs when blood supply to a part of the brain is interrupted or when a blood vessel in the brain ruptures. Recognising the symptoms and seeking immediate medical attention are crucial to reducing complications and improving recovery. The session will examine emerging approaches to stroke diagnosis and management, along with the importance of reaching a healthcare facility equipped to provide appropriate treatment.

Sivarajan Thandeswaran, senior consultant in Stroke Medicine, General Internal Medicine and Gerontology, Kauvery Hospital, Alwarpet, Chennai, will discuss advances in treatment and emerging approaches to stroke management.

Harish R. Kamath, consultant neurologist, Kauvery Hospital, Hosur, will explain how to recognise stroke symptoms, why immediate medical intervention is essential, and how timely access to the right healthcare facility can affect outcomes.
Registration is open at https://newsth.live/THKAGE or scan the QR code below.

articles.title: UK approves J&J's oral psoriasis pill
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: In all four studies, patients who took the drug saw better results after 16 weeks than those given a placebo, the regulator said

Britain’s medicines regulator on Friday approved Johnson & Johnson’s daily pill for adults and teenagers with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, a skin condition causing red, scaly and often itchy or painful patches.

The Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) approved the oral drug Icotyde for people aged 12 and older who weigh at least 40 kg. The approval was based on four late-stage trials in 2,500 people with the disease, including 72 teenagers aged 12 to under 18. In all four studies, patients who took the drug saw better results after 16 weeks than those given a placebo, the regulator said.

Icotyde was approved in the U.S. earlier this year for the same condition — its first approved indication. The drug is made in collaboration with Protagonist Therapeutics. J&J is also studying the drug, chemically known as icotrokinra, for ulcerative colitis, psoriatic arthritis and Crohn’s disease.

The company expects the treatment to bring in $5 billion in peak sales across multiple indications. The drug competes with established psoriasis treatments such as Bristol Myers Squibb’s Sotyktu and AbbVie’s blockbuster Skyrizi.

articles.title: How peripheral artery disease is treated as leg pain worsens
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Treatment for PAD includes medicines, structured exercise and procedures to improve blood flow. Experts advise patients not to push through severe pain during exercise and to seek medical advice if pain occurs

For people living with peripheral artery disease (PAD), walking even short distances or doing routine household tasks can become difficult because of leg pain. The condition develops when arteries supplying blood to the legs become narrow, usually because fatty deposits build up along their walls. With less blood reaching the muscles, walking can cause pain, cramps or heaviness that ease with rest. In advanced cases, pain may persist even when a person is sitting or lying down, and poor circulation can lead to wounds that do not heal.

Treatment can be challenging too because movement is an important part of managing PAD, while pain makes it difficult to stay active. Structured exercise, medicines and control of risk factors such as smoking, diabetes and high blood pressure can help manage the condition. When blood flow is severely reduced, procedures may be needed to prevent damage to the feet and legs. PAD can also affect overall cardiovascular health, increasing the risk of heart attack and stroke.

Pain, cramps, heaviness in the calf or thigh that develop during walking and ease with rest are known as intermittent claudication. This happens when narrowed arteries cannot supply enough blood to meet the muscles’ increased needs during activity.

Venu S., consultant vascular surgeon, Prashanth Hospitals, Chennai, says structured walking programmes can help patients gradually increase the distance they can walk. Patients are generally advised to walk until the discomfort becomes moderate, rest until it settles and then resume walking. Sessions commonly last 30 to 45 minutes and take place several times a week, with supervision where possible.

He says patients who follow a structured programme for about three months may be able to walk twice as far, or more, before pain begins. The pace and duration should suit each patient’s ability. Those who find walking difficult may need an adapted exercise programme under medical supervision.

Balaji V., senior consultant, vascular surgery, Apollo Hospitals, Greams Road, Chennai, says quitting smoking, eating a healthy diet, staying physically active and controlling blood sugar, blood pressure and cholesterol are also important parts of treatment.

Exercise should not mean pushing through severe pain. Pain that does not settle with rest needs medical assessment. Pain in the feet or toes while resting, particularly at night, can indicate a serious reduction in blood flow and requires prompt medical attention.

Diagnosis usually begins with a review of symptoms and medical history, followed by an examination of the legs and feet, including checking the pulses. Doctors may measure the ankle-brachial index (ABI), which compares blood pressure at the ankle with that in the arm, to assess blood flow. A Doppler ultrasound scan can help identify narrowed arteries and assess circulation. In patients with severe symptoms or wounds that do not heal, a CT angiogram may be needed to locate the blockage and plan treatment.

Medicines aim to relieve symptoms, slow the progression of arterial disease and reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke. PAD can also affect overall cardiovascular health, increasing the risk of heart attack and stroke.

Pain, cramps, heaviness in the calf or thigh that develop during walking and ease with rest are known as intermittent claudication. This happens when narrowed arteries cannot supply enough blood to meet the muscles’ increased needs during activity.

Patients are generally advised to walk until the discomfort becomes moderate, rest until it settles and then resume walking. articles.title: What is the controversy over the spinal muscular atrophy drug in Keralam? Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: After the government switched the drug in its SMA programme from branded to generic, parents of children living with SMA have been asking for a switch back to the branded version; meanwhile the label on a drug bottle has sparked concerns, and political parties have now latched on to the issue
An initiative launched by Keralam government to make the treatment for Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) accessible to more patients is now courting controversy .

SMA is a rare, life-threatening genetic disorder that progressively weakens muscles, severely impairing both mobility and respiratory function. While a complete cure remains elusive, the launch of Risdiplam, marketed as Evrysdi by Roche Pharmaceuticals, the first at-home, oral treatment for SMA, gave hope to thousands of SMA patients. Risdiplam was found to have a significant effect on the progression of the disease, by slowing down motor degeneration, improving physical milestones and stabilising respiratory function.
Risdiplam was launched in India in July 2021, making it the first and only approved drug in the country to manage SMA. But the drug’s astronomical cost made it inaccessible to most families.

Keralam, which has been giving Risdiplam free of cost to eligible children since 2022, made a switch to the less expensive generic version of the drug in October this year . But since then, a section of parents of children living with SMA children have urged the government to switch back to the expensive, branded version.

Last week, when the generic drug was dispensed for the first time at SAT hospital, a Centre of Excellence for Rare Diseases in Thiruvananthapuram, a sticker on the bottle which said “Physicians’ sample/for clinical trials” reopened the branded versus generic debate and a new allegation , that drugs meant for clinical trials were being used on children

Keralam was the first State to give Risdiplam free of cost through government hospitals in 2022 and an SMA clinic was subsequently opened at SAT hospital. Though initially Risdiplam was given free only to children under 12, in 2026 the government announced an extension of coverage to genetically confirmed SMA Type 2 patients up to age 25, with ₹30 crore allocated in the State budget for this. However, as of now, 109 Type 1 and 2 children with SMA below the age of 12 are being given Risdiplam, free.

Risdiplam, under its trade name Evrysdi, used to cost ₹6.3 lakh for a bottle (current price ₹4.44 lakhs), which the State was getting at a negotiated price of ₹5.4 lakh per bottle. Under the patient assistance programme, Roche used to give 11 bottles free of cost to the State for every four bottles it purchased. The State’s annual requirement was estimated at around 2,500 bottles and the annual financial commitment was around ₹23 crore. The State, therefore, was up against enormous cumulative expenditure as more children became eligible and existing patients required continued treatment.

A technical experts committee in Keralam met several times to evaluate if the generic alternative, Natsmart , which has all regulatory approvals, and which was ready for commercial distribution in October 2025, could replace Roche’s Evrysdi. Natco Pharma, through a historic Delhi High Court verdict , had won the right to marker the generic alternative of Risdiplam at a dramatically reduced price of ₹15,900 per bottle, against Roche’s Rs. 6.3 lakhs per bottle.

A bottle of Evrysdi on which Roche holds a patent, typically lasts 12 days, meaning the annual maintenance cost for a patient would amount to a crushing ₹60-70 lakh. With Natsmart, the generic alternative, the cost would be under ₹5 lakh. In February 2026, the Keralam government gave the go ahead for Natsmart, and purchase processes were initiated.

Parents and advocacy groups including the Cure SMA Foundation of India claim that the branded medication, Evrysdi, has a proven, long-term track record of safety and efficacy, while the new generic version lacks dedicated human bioequivalence or long-term clinical studies specific to paediatric patients. They claim that a sudden switch to an unverified or less effective generic formula could reverse the critical motor and survival progress already achieved by children who are currently stable on the original drug. They have been continuously petitioning the government asking that their children be allowed to continue on Evrysdi.

Public health experts have hailed the government’s decision to switch to the generic drug. They say that arguments challenging the efficacy of the generic formulation and alleging a lack of ‘bioavailability’ are entirely unscientific and baseless.

Bioavailability denotes the rate and extent to which an administered pharmaceutical substance enters systemic circulation through the digestive tract. A bioequivalence study normally compares the rate and extent of absorption of the generic with the reference product. The World Health Organization (WHO) recognises this as an important way to establish interchangeability. However, bioequivalence studies are not required for every generic medicine. The WHO’s guidance on generic medicines explicitly recognises circumstances in which equivalence studies can be waived. One such circumstance is when the generic and reference products are pharmaceutically equivalent oral solutions containing the same active ingredient at the same molar concentration, subject to the applicable requirements for excipients.

articles.title: Why is Qualcomm cutting jobs? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: According to CEO Cristiano Amon, the decision stems from the company’s evolving needs as it expands into new domains

Qualcomm announced global job cuts , framing the layoffs as a “performance-focused reduction,” the Reuters reported. According to CEO Cristiano Amon, the decision stems from the company’s evolving needs as it expands into new domains.

While internal messaging presents these cuts as a routine alignment of talent and role competencies, the underlying drivers are rooted in severe macroeconomic headwinds, an over-reliance on a declining smartphone market, delayed returns on diversification, key customer account vulnerabilities, and board impatience during a multi-year corporate transformation.
However, we still do not know how many jobs will be axed in the coming months, and which regions will be most impacted by the layoffs.

The primary external trigger for Qualcomm’s restructuring is the sharp downturn in global smartphone sales . According to Counterpoint Research, global smartphone shipments dropped 20% year-over-year (YoY) in Q3 2026, marking the lowest market levels since 2012.
This drop was heavily fuelled by soaring memory chip prices, which inflated the bill of materials (BOM) costs for Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) and exacerbated supply shortages.
In response, OEMs passed on these cost increases to consumers, driving global smartphone retail prices up by 20% so far in 2026 and lifting average selling prices (ASPs).

However, higher price tags have failed to offset volume declines. In key growth markets such as India, market research firm Techarc projects 2026 to close down 26–28% by volume and 7–8% by value compared to 2025.
When a major volume driver like India experiences such severe contraction, the entire semiconductor value chain, and especially component suppliers like Qualcomm, feels the impact.

Smartphones remain Qualcomm’s single largest revenue driver, accounting for 51% of total revenue, according to its latest financial reporting. Because more than half of its top line is tied to a single product category, Qualcomm remains acutely vulnerable to contractions in consumer mobile demand.

While Qualcomm has actively pursued diversification, non-smartphone categories have been slow to yield significant financial scale. In the automotive sector, Qualcomm has gained solid traction, but building a material revenue contribution takes time. At best, automotive is projected to settle at 25–30% of Qualcomm’s total revenue within the next 3 to 5 years.
The efforts to expand into PC chips and laptops have been slow to gain mass-market momentum.

Emerging categories like smart eyewear present significant long-term promise, but achieving scale requires strong penetration into mass consumer price tiers (such as the ₹10,000–15,000 range in India), rather than remaining confined to niche premium offerings like Ray-Ban Meta or Oakley Meta.

articles.title: Notify Pallikaranai under Wetlands Rules, 2017: Sowmiya Anbumani
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: She alleges that the CMDA’s approval of buildings over natural drainage channels and waterways is itself a serious violation of the law

PMK floor leader Sowmiya Anbumani on Tuesday urged the Tamil Nadu State Wetlands Authority to immediately notify Pallikaranai marshland under the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017, and include all 65 water bodies flowing into the marshlands within its zone of influence.

In a letter submitted to Rakesh Kumar Jageniya, Member Secretary, Tamil Nadu State Wetlands Authority in Chennai, Ms. Sowmiya demanded that the newly constructed compound wall and walkway on the marshland be removed.
Aerial view of Pallikaranai marshland, a Ramsar site. | Photo Credit: JOTHI RAMALINGAM B

“Construction companies planning to build large structures in the zone of influence of Pallikaranai Ramsar Wetland appear to want to block the waterways that bring water to the wetland and prevent the flow of water so that they can construct buildings. Several major construction companies have already built structures over drainage channels, leaving passages beneath the buildings for water to flow. The CMDA’s approval of buildings over natural drainage channels and waterways is itself a serious violation of the law,” she charged.

Major construction companies are reportedly planning to encroach upon areas surrounding the 65 water bodies in the Pallikaranai watershed, as well as the channels through which the water flows. “This could well be the real reason why construction companies are demanding a reduction in the area designated as the zone of influence of the wetland. A wetland and its zone of influence are not the same. Under the 2017 Rules, permanent construction is prohibited within the notified wetland boundary. The same blanket prohibition does not apply to the zone of influence outside the wetland,” she said.

She alleges that the CMDA’s approval of buildings over natural drainage channels and waterways is itself a serious violation of the law

PMK floor leader Sowmiya Anbumani on Tuesday urged the Tamil Nadu State Wetlands Authority to immediately notify Pallikaranai marshland under the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017, and include all 65 water bodies flowing into the marshlands within its zone of influence.

In a letter submitted to Rakesh Kumar Jageniya, Member Secretary, Tamil Nadu State Wetlands Authority in Chennai, Ms. Sowmiya demanded that the newly constructed compound wall and walkway on the marshland be removed.

Aerial view of Pallikaranai marshland, a Ramsar site. | Photo Credit: JOTHI RAMALINGAM B

“Construction companies planning to build large structures in the zone of influence of Pallikaranai Ramsar Wetland appear to want to block the waterways that bring water to the wetland and prevent the flow of water so that they can construct buildings. Several major construction companies have already built structures over drainage channels, leaving passages beneath the buildings for water to flow. The CMDA’s approval of buildings over natural drainage channels and waterways is itself a serious violation of the law,” she charged.

Major construction companies are reportedly planning to encroach upon areas surrounding the 65 water bodies in the Pallikaranai watershed, as well as the channels through which the water flows. “This could well be the real reason why construction companies are demanding a reduction in the area designated as the zone of influence of the wetland. A wetland and its zone of influence are not the same. Under the 2017 Rules, permanent construction is prohibited within the notified wetland boundary. The same blanket prohibition does not apply to the zone of influence outside the wetland,” she said.
